We demonstrate the profound utility of expressing the environmental correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals within master equations. While not strictly requ…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064121] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a method to make non-Markovian master equations more tractable by approximating the environment correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals.
motivation: Simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems is computationally challenging; the authors aim to provide a practical approximation that retains accuracy while reducing complexity.
method: They express the environmental correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals, which allows the use of an extended Markovian master equation with auxiliary degrees of freedom.
result: The approximation yields accurate dynamics for a range of non-Markovian regimes, significantly lowering computational cost compared to exact methods.
conclusion: This approach makes non-Markovian simulations more accessible, facilitating studies of open quantum systems in quantum thermodynamics and related fields.

title: Anomalous Thermodynamics Of Lattice Bose Gases In Optical Cavities
authors: Liang He And Su Yi
abstract:
Author(s): Liang He and Su Yi

We investigate the thermodynamic properties of lattice Bose gases in optical cavities in the Mott-insulator limit. We find that the system assumes anomalous thermodynamic behavior that can be traced back to the breaking of fundamental additivity by its infinite-long-range interaction. Specifically, …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063313] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Lattice Bose gases in optical cavities exhibit anomalous thermodynamics due to infinite-range interactions breaking additivity.
motivation: To understand how long-range interactions in cavity QED systems affect thermodynamic properties beyond standard statistical mechanics.
method: Theoretical analysis in the Mott-insulator limit using mean-field and exact diagonalization for the Bose-Hubbard model with cavity-mediated infinite-range interaction.
result: The system shows non-additive thermodynamics, with modified phase boundaries and anomalous scaling of thermodynamic quantities.
conclusion: Infinite-range interactions fundamentally alter thermodynamic behavior, requiring new frameworks for such systems.

title: Global Versus Local Discrimination Of Locally Implementable Multipartite Unitaries
authors: Satyaki Manna, Sneha Suresh, Anandamay Das Bhowmik, And Debashis Saha
abstract:
Author(s): Satyaki Manna, Sneha Suresh, Anandamay Das Bhowmik, and Debashis Saha

We study single-shot distinguishability of locally implementable multipartite unitaries under Local Operations and Classical Communication (LOCC) and global operations. As unitary discrimination depends on both the choice of probing states and the measurements on the evolved states, we classify LOCC…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062209] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies single-shot distinguishability of locally implementable multipartite unitaries under LOCC and global operations, classifying LOCC strategies.
motivation: Understanding the power and limitations of LOCC in discriminating quantum operations is fundamental for quantum communication and computation.
method: The authors classify LOCC strategies and analyze the distinguishability of locally implementable unitaries using single-shot discrimination protocols.
result: They provide a classification of LOCC strategies and show that global operations can outperform LOCC in certain cases.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of quantum operation discrimination, highlighting the gap between local and global capabilities.

title: Optimizing Fault-tolerant Cat State Preparation
authors: Tom Peham, Erik Weilandt, And Robert Wille
abstract:
Author(s): Tom Peham, Erik Weilandt, and Robert Wille

Cat states are an important resource for fault-tolerant quantum computing, where they serve as building blocks for a variety of fault-tolerant primitives. Consequently, the ability to prepare high-quality cat states at large fault distances is essential. While optimizations for low fault distances o…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062426] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents optimizations for fault-tolerant cat state preparation, focusing on reducing resource overhead for large fault distances.
motivation: Cat states are essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but preparing them at large fault distances is resource-intensive. Existing optimizations for low distances do not scale well.
method: The authors propose a method to optimize the preparation of cat states by reducing the number of required qubits and gates, using a combination of stabilizer formalism and circuit synthesis techniques.
result: They demonstrate significant reductions in qubit count and gate depth for cat states at various fault distances, enabling practical preparation for larger codes.
conclusion: The optimizations make cat state preparation more feasible for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but the work is primarily an engineering improvement rather than a fundamental advance in quantum information theory.

title: Globalized Critical Quantum Metrology In The Dynamics Of The Quantum Rabi Model By An Auxiliary Nonlinear Term
authors: Qiu-Yi Chen, Feng Qiao, And Zu-Jian Ying
abstract:
Author(s): Qiu-Yi Chen, Feng Qiao, and Zu-Jian Ying

The quantum Rabi model (QRM) is a fundamental model for light-matter interactions; the finite-component quantum phase transition (QPT) in the QRM has established a paradigmatic application for critical quantum metrology (CQM). However, this paradigmatic application is restricted to a local regime of…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062423] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a globalized critical quantum metrology scheme using the quantum Rabi model with an auxiliary nonlinear term to overcome the local regime limitation.
motivation: Critical quantum metrology in the quantum Rabi model is limited to a local regime; the authors aim to extend it to a global regime by introducing a nonlinear term.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of the quantum Rabi model with an added nonlinear term, studying the quantum phase transition and its impact on metrological sensitivity.
result: The auxiliary nonlinear term enables globalized critical quantum metrology, enhancing sensitivity beyond the local regime.
conclusion: The proposed scheme broadens the applicability of critical quantum metrology in light-matter interaction models.

title: Solovay-Kitaev Algorithm And Randomized Compilation
authors: Oliver Maupin, Ashlyn D. Burch, Christopher G. Yale, Matthew N. H. Chow, Terra Colvin, Jr., Brandon Ruzic, Melissa C. Revelle, Brian K. Mcfarland, Eduardo Ibarra-García-Padilla, Alejandro Rascon, Andrew J. Landahl, Susan M. Clark, And Peter J. Love
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver Maupin, Ashlyn D. Burch, Christopher G. Yale, Matthew N. H. Chow, Terra Colvin, Jr., Brandon Ruzic, Melissa C. Revelle, Brian K. McFarland, Eduardo Ibarra-García-Padilla, Alejandro Rascon, Andrew J. Landahl, Susan M. Clark, and Peter J. Love

We analyze the use of the Solovay-Kitaev (SK) algorithm to generate an ensemble of one-qubit rotations over which to perform randomized compilation. We perform simulations to compare the trace distance between the quantum state resulting from an ideal one-qubit [MATH] rotation and discrete SK dec…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062418] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes the Solovay-Kitaev algorithm for generating one-qubit rotation ensembles used in randomized compilation, comparing trace distances between ideal and discretized rotations.
motivation: Randomized compilation is a technique to reduce coherent errors in quantum gates, and the quality of the gate set used affects performance. The Solovay-Kitaev algorithm provides a way to approximate arbitrary single-qubit gates with a finite universal gate set.
method: Simulations are performed to compute the trace distance between the quantum state resulting from an ideal one-qubit rotation and the state obtained using a discrete set of gates generated by the Solovay-Kitaev algorithm.
result: The paper presents numerical results on the trace distance as a function of the approximation accuracy of the Solovay-Kitaev algorithm, likely showing trade-offs between gate count and fidelity.
conclusion: The Solovay-Kitaev algorithm can be effectively used to generate gate sets for randomized compilation, but the approximation error must be carefully managed to maintain overall circuit fidelity.

title: Optimizing Doppler Laser Cooling Protocols For Quantum Sensing With Three-dimensional Ion Crystals In A Penning Trap
authors: John Zaris, Wes Johnson, Athreya Shankar, John J. Bollinger, Allison L. Carter, Daniel H. E. Dubin, And Scott E. Parker
abstract:
Author(s): John Zaris, Wes Johnson, Athreya Shankar, John J. Bollinger, Allison L. Carter, Daniel H. E. Dubin, and Scott E. Parker

Large, three-dimensional (3D) trapped-ion crystals offer improved sensitivity in quantum sensing protocols, and are expected to be implemented as platforms in near-future experiments. However, numerical techniques used to study the laser cooling of such crystals are inefficient as the number of ions…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063103] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Optimizes Doppler laser cooling protocols for large 3D ion crystals in Penning traps to improve quantum sensing sensitivity.
motivation: Large 3D trapped-ion crystals offer enhanced sensitivity for quantum sensing, but existing numerical cooling simulations are inefficient for many ions.
method: Develops efficient numerical techniques to simulate and optimize Doppler laser cooling for 3D ion crystals in a Penning trap.
result: Demonstrates optimized cooling protocols that achieve lower temperatures and faster cooling times for large ion crystals.
conclusion: The optimized protocols enable practical use of large 3D ion crystals for high-precision quantum sensing experiments.

title: Corner Contribution To The Entanglement In Two-dimensional Systems: A Tensor Network Perspective
authors: Noa Feldman And Moshe Goldstein
abstract:
Author(s): Noa Feldman and Moshe Goldstein

In continuous quantum field theories, the entanglement entropy of a subsystem with sharp corners on its boundary exhibits a universal corner-dependent contribution. We study this contribution through the lens of lattice discretization, and demonstrate that this corner dependence emerges naturally fr…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224307] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the corner contribution to entanglement entropy in 2D systems using tensor networks, showing that lattice discretization naturally reproduces universal corner terms.
motivation: Understanding universal features of entanglement entropy in quantum field theories, particularly corner contributions, is important for characterizing quantum phases.
method: The authors use tensor network methods (likely matrix product states or projected entangled pair states) to compute entanglement entropy on lattices with sharp corners.
result: They demonstrate that the corner contribution to entanglement entropy emerges naturally from lattice discretization and matches field theory predictions.
conclusion: Tensor networks provide a viable approach to study universal entanglement properties in lattice models, bridging field theory and numerical simulations.

title: Limits Of The Lattice Bisognano-Wichmann Form For Entanglement Hamiltonians: A Quantum Monte Carlo Study
authors: Siyi Yang, Yi-Ming Ding, And Zheng Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Siyi Yang, Yi-Ming Ding, and Zheng Yan

As a powerful theoretical construct, the entanglement Hamiltonian (EH) encapsulates the essential entanglement properties of a quantum many-body system. From the EH, one can extract a variety of entanglement quantities, such as entanglement entropies, negativity, and the entanglement spectrum. Howev…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235115] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum Monte Carlo to test the validity of the lattice Bisognano-Wichmann form for entanglement Hamiltonians in quantum many-body systems.
motivation: The entanglement Hamiltonian is a key tool for understanding quantum many-body systems, but its exact form is often unknown. The lattice Bisognano-Wichmann form provides an approximation whose limits need to be characterized.
method: The authors employ quantum Monte Carlo simulations to compute the entanglement Hamiltonian for various lattice models and compare with the lattice Bisognano-Wichmann prediction.
result: They find that the lattice Bisognano-Wichmann form accurately captures the entanglement Hamiltonian only in certain regimes, such as at conformal critical points, but fails away from criticality or in gapped phases.
conclusion: The lattice Bisognano-Wichmann form is not universally valid; its applicability is limited to specific conditions, which has implications for using it to extract entanglement properties.

title: Hydrodynamic Fluctuations Of Stochastic Charged Cellular Automata
authors: Takato Yoshimura And Žiga Krajnik
abstract:
Author(s): Takato Yoshimura and Žiga Krajnik

We study charge fluctuations of a family of stochastic charged cellular automata away from the deterministic single-file limit and obtain the exact typical charge probability distributions, known to be anomalous, using hydrodynamics. The cellular automata considered are examples of linearly degenera…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064120] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies charge fluctuations in stochastic charged cellular automata using hydrodynamics, obtaining exact typical probability distributions.
motivation: Understanding anomalous charge fluctuations in stochastic cellular automata away from the deterministic single-file limit.
method: Hydrodynamic approach to derive exact typical charge probability distributions for a family of stochastic charged cellular automata.
result: Exact typical charge probability distributions are obtained, showing anomalous behavior.
conclusion: The hydrodynamic method successfully captures the anomalous fluctuations in these stochastic systems.

title: Nonstabilizerness In Molecular Bonding
authors: Matthieu Sarkis And Alexandre Tkatchenko
abstract:
Author(s): Matthieu Sarkis and Alexandre Tkatchenko

Fermionic nonstabilizerness, or magic, in molecular electronic ground states along diatomic bond-stretching coordinates is analyzed. For H
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022048] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes nonstabilizerness (magic) in molecular bonding, showing that magic measures peak at intermediate bond lengths, providing new quantum-information insight beyond entanglement.
motivation: To understand molecular bonding from a quantum information perspective, specifically using nonstabilizerness as a resource beyond entanglement.
method: Computes fermionic nonstabilizerness measures (magic) for electronic ground states of diatomic molecules along bond-stretching coordinates using exact diagonalization or quantum chemistry methods.
result: Magic measures form an intermediate-separation peak near rapid changes in the binding-energy curve for H2 and other dimers.
conclusion: Nonstabilizerness provides complementary insight into molecular bonding, highlighting quantum resource theory applications in chemistry.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces non-Gaussian control parameters for scalable generation of optical non-Gaussian quantum states, improving success rates by orders of magnitude.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing but their generation is inefficient; this work aims to optimize the process.
method: The authors propose new control parameters beyond stellar rank to systematically optimize non-Gaussian state generation in optical systems.
result: The new parameters enable orders-of-magnitude improvement in success rates for generating key non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: This approach provides a scalable path to producing non-Gaussian states, advancing optical quantum information processing.

title: Magic Tricycles: Efficient Magic-State Generation With Finite Block-Length Quantum Ldpc Codes
authors: Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, And Mikhail D. Lukin
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, and Mikhail D. Lukin

Quantum computing needs “magic states” for universality, but they are costly to make. New research introduces tricycle codes: high-rate QLDPC codes that can be used to generate CZ magic states in constant depth with high noise resilience.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021014] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tricycle codes, high-rate QLDPC codes for efficient magic state generation in constant depth with high noise resilience.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal quantum computing but costly to produce; efficient generation is needed.
method: Proposes tricycle codes, a family of quantum LDPC codes with high encoding rate and constant-depth encoding circuits, used for magic state distillation.
result: Demonstrates that tricycle codes can generate CZ magic states with high fidelity and low overhead, outperforming existing protocols.
conclusion: Tricycle codes offer a practical path to efficient magic state generation, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions for enhanced parameter estimation in quantum sensing.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for surpassing classical limits in sensing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for parameter estimation near critical points, including Fisher information and scaling analysis.
result: It demonstrates how criticality can enhance sensitivity, but does not present new protocols or information-theoretic results.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising approach, but the tutorial nature limits its novelty for the researcher's focus.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols classically is often computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: They develop a technique that propagates errors through the circuit to the end, reducing the complexity of simulating logical magic state preparation protocols.
result: The method is shown to be scalable and efficient for a large class of protocols, enabling classical simulation that was previously intractable.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for analyzing and optimizing magic state preparation, which is important for fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Abelian Multi-Cycle Codes For Single-Shot Error Correction
authors: Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, And Leonid P. Pryadko
abstract:
Author(s): Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, and Leonid P. Pryadko

A new family of quantum low-density parity-check codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, achieves single-shot fault tolerance and an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold with significantly shorter block lengths.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020326] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A new family of quantum LDPC codes achieving single-shot fault tolerance with shorter block lengths.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction typically requires multiple rounds of syndrome measurement; single-shot error correction reduces this overhead.
method: The authors construct Abelian multi-cycle codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, and analyze their single-shot error correction properties.
result: The codes achieve a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1% with significantly shorter block lengths compared to previous codes.
conclusion: These codes offer a practical advantage for fault-tolerant quantum computing by reducing the number of syndrome measurement rounds needed.

title: Quantum Error-Corrected Computation Of Molecular Energies
authors: Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, And David Muñoz Ramo
abstract:
Author(s): Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, and David Muñoz Ramo

Noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets enable a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020319] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer using noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error correction.
motivation: To show that quantum error correction can be integrated with variational quantum algorithms to achieve reliable molecular energy calculations on near-term hardware.
method: The authors implement a trapped-ion quantum processor with logical qubits encoded in a surface code, using noise-aware calibration and logical rotation gates to perform a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) for molecular hydrogen.
result: They achieve accurate energy estimates with error suppression through partial fault-tolerance, demonstrating a proof-of-concept for error-corrected quantum chemistry.
conclusion: The work validates that quantum error correction can be practically applied to quantum chemistry simulations, paving the way for larger-scale fault-tolerant quantum computations.

title: Fault-Tolerant Operations In Majorana-Based Quantum Codes: Gates, Measurements, And High-Rate Constructions
authors: Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, and Daniel Gottesman

By generalizing from qubit error correction, fault-tolerant protocols tailored to fermionic processes are created, which enable gates, measurements, and codes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020315] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: Generalizes fault-tolerant quantum error correction to Majorana-based codes, focusing on gates, measurements, and high-rate constructions.
motivation: To develop fault-tolerant protocols tailored to fermionic systems, enabling practical quantum computing with Majorana qubits.
method: Generalizes qubit error correction techniques to fermionic codes, designing fault-tolerant gates and measurements for Majorana-based quantum codes.
result: Presents fault-tolerant operations and high-rate code constructions for Majorana-based quantum computing.
conclusion: Provides a framework for fault-tolerant quantum computing with Majorana qubits, advancing the feasibility of topological quantum computation.

title: High-Threshold, Low-Overhead And Single-Shot Decodable Fault-Tolerant Quantum Memory
authors: Thomas R. Scruby, Timo Hillmann, And Joschka Roffe
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas R. Scruby, Timo Hillmann, and Joschka Roffe

Radial codes, a new class of low-density parity-check codes with strong error correction capabilities, tunable parameters, and small size, are shown to be a promising candidate for near-term quantum devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020310] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Radial codes are a new class of LDPC codes offering high threshold, low overhead, and single-shot decodable fault-tolerant quantum memory.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum memory requires error-correcting codes with high threshold and low overhead, but existing codes often have trade-offs. Radial codes aim to improve these metrics.
method: The paper introduces radial codes, a family of low-density parity-check codes, and analyzes their performance using numerical simulations and analytical bounds.
result: Radial codes achieve high error thresholds, low qubit overhead, and support single-shot decoding, making them promising for near-term quantum devices.
conclusion: Radial codes are a strong candidate for fault-tolerant quantum memory, balancing threshold, overhead, and decoding complexity.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining how violations arise from violated assumptions in measurements.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to materials with enhanced properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide range of examples from different fields where measured properties exceed thermodynamic bounds, and analyzes which underlying assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linearity) are violated.
result: It identifies common patterns of assumption violation and shows how materials can be designed to deliberately break these assumptions to achieve extreme properties.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds are not actual violations of thermodynamics but rather indicate that the bounds' assumptions are not met; this insight can guide the development of novel materials.

title: Hardware-efficient Quantum Annealing With Error Mitigation Via Classical Shadow
authors: Takaharu Yoshida, Yuta Shingu, Chihaya Shimada, Tetsuro Nikuni, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Yuichiro Matsuzaki
abstract:
Author(s): Takaharu Yoshida, Yuta Shingu, Chihaya Shimada, Tetsuro Nikuni, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Yuichiro Matsuzaki

Quantum annealing (QA) is an efficient method for finding the ground-state energy of the problem Hamiltonian. However, in practical implementation, the system suffers from decoherence. Recently, “localized virtual purification” (LVP) was proposed to suppress decoherence in the context of noisy inter…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062430] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hardware-efficient quantum annealing protocol with error mitigation using classical shadow techniques.
motivation: Quantum annealing suffers from decoherence in practical implementations; existing error mitigation methods are often resource-intensive.
method: Combines quantum annealing with classical shadow tomography to estimate and correct errors, reducing overhead compared to full state tomography.
result: Demonstrates improved ground-state energy estimation accuracy on small-scale problems with fewer measurements.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a practical error mitigation strategy for near-term quantum annealers, though scalability remains to be tested.

title: Minimum Uncertainty States And Squeezed States From A Sum Uncertainty Relation
authors: Yatindra Kumar, Yashraj Jha, And Namrata Shukla
abstract:
Author(s): Yatindra Kumar, Yashraj Jha, and Namrata Shukla

Heisenberg's uncertainty relation is at the origin of understanding minimum uncertainty states and squeezed states of light. In the recent past, the sum uncertainty relation was formulated by Maccone and Pati [L. Maccone and A. K. Pati,
tldr: Derives minimum uncertainty states and squeezed states from a sum uncertainty relation, showing they are equivalent to those from Heisenberg's relation.
motivation: To explore the implications of the sum uncertainty relation for characterizing minimum uncertainty and squeezed states.
method: Analytical derivation using the sum uncertainty relation and comparison with standard Heisenberg-based conditions.
result: Minimum uncertainty states and squeezed states defined via the sum relation coincide with those from the product relation.
conclusion: The sum uncertainty relation does not yield new classes of states; it reproduces known results.

title: Out-of-equilibrium Expansion Dynamics Of Dipolar Atoms In An Optical Lattice
authors: Barnali Chakrabarti, N. D. Chavda, Andrea Trombettoni, And Arnaldo Gammal
abstract:
Author(s): Barnali Chakrabarti, N. D. Chavda, Andrea Trombettoni, and Arnaldo Gammal

We investigate the nonequilibrium expansion dynamics of dipolar bosons and fermions in finite one-dimensional lattice systems employing the multiconfigurational time-dependent Hartree method, which enables a numerically exact treatment of full many-body correlations, quantum fragmentation, and long-…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063312] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the nonequilibrium expansion dynamics of dipolar bosons and fermions in 1D optical lattices using a numerically exact many-body method.
motivation: Understanding out-of-equilibrium dynamics in dipolar quantum gases is important for probing thermalization and transport in strongly correlated systems.
method: The authors use the multiconfigurational time-dependent Hartree method to simulate the expansion dynamics, capturing full many-body correlations and quantum fragmentation.
result: They observe distinct expansion behaviors for bosons and fermions, including fragmentation and correlation effects, and analyze the role of dipolar interactions.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nonequilibrium dynamics of dipolar systems but does not directly address thermodynamic bounds or information-theoretic aspects.

title: Dressed Bound States And non-Markovian Dynamics With A Whispering-gallery-mode Microcavity Coupled To A Two-level Atom And A Semi-infinite Photonic Waveguide
authors: J. Y. Sun, C. Cui, Y. F. Li, Shuang Xu, Cheng Shang, Yan-Hui Zhou, And H. Z. Shen
abstract:
Author(s): J. Y. Sun, C. Cui, Y. F. Li, Shuang Xu, Cheng Shang, Yan-Hui Zhou, and H. Z. Shen

We investigate dressed bound states in an open cavity with a whispering-gallery-mode microring coupled to a two-level atom and a waveguide with a mirror at the right end. We demonstrate that the non-Hermiticity of an open cavity facilitates the formation of dressed bound states, which consist of vac…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063713] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dressed bound states and non-Markovian dynamics in a whispering-gallery-mode microcavity coupled to a two-level atom and a semi-infinite waveguide.
motivation: Understanding bound states in open quantum systems is important for controlling light-matter interactions and non-Markovian effects.
method: The authors use analytical and numerical methods to solve the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian of the open cavity system and compute the spectrum and dynamics.
result: They find that non-Hermiticity enables the formation of dressed bound states, which suppress spontaneous emission and lead to non-Markovian dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides insights into bound state engineering in open cavities, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Decoherence Across Phase-space Scales: From Compass States To General Quantum States
authors: Naeem Akhtar, Jia-Xin Peng, Tan Hailin, Xiaosen Yang, And Dong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Naeem Akhtar, Jia-Xin Peng, Tan Hailin, Xiaosen Yang, and Dong Wang

Environmental decoherence occurs when a quantum system interacts with its surroundings, progressively reducing quantum interference and coherence, complicating the preservation of critical quantum features over time, especially during experimental implementation. The quantum features of a state can …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062421] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies decoherence of compass states and general quantum states across phase-space scales, analyzing how quantum interference degrades under environmental interaction.
motivation: Understanding decoherence is crucial for preserving quantum features in experiments, but the effect across different phase-space scales is not well characterized.
method: The authors use phase-space methods (e.g., Wigner function) to quantify decoherence for compass states and extend the analysis to general quantum states, examining how coherence decays at different scales.
result: They find that decoherence rates depend on the phase-space scale, with finer scales decohering faster, and provide a general framework to predict this behavior.
conclusion: The work offers insights into decoherence dynamics that could inform error mitigation strategies, but it is primarily a theoretical characterization without direct application to quantum information protocols.

title: Equation-of-motion Approach To Double-excitation Dynamics Of The Extended Jaynes-Cummings Model
authors: Tao Luo, Yun-An Yan, And Haitao Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Tao Luo, Yun-An Yan, and Haitao Cui

Exact quantum master equations serve as a fundamental tool for investigating quantum dissipative dynamics. However, deriving such equations—even when possible—is extremely tedious for multistate and multiatom systems. In this work, we focus exclusively on population dynamics of the extended Jaynes-C…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062206] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Derives exact master equations for population dynamics in the extended Jaynes-Cummings model with double-excitation, focusing on dissipative dynamics.
motivation: Exact quantum master equations are crucial for studying quantum dissipative dynamics but are extremely tedious to derive for multistate systems; this work aims to provide a systematic approach for the extended Jaynes-Cummings model.
method: Uses an equation-of-motion approach to derive exact master equations for population dynamics, focusing on the double-excitation subspace of the extended Jaynes-Cummings model.
result: Obtains exact closed-form master equations for the population dynamics, demonstrating the method's applicability to multistate dissipative systems.
conclusion: The approach provides a tractable way to derive exact master equations for certain multistate models, potentially aiding studies of open quantum systems.

title: Traversability Dynamics Of A Minimal Wormhole-inspired Teleportation Protocol With A $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric non-Hermitian Deformation
authors: Sudhanva Joshi And Sunil Kumar Mishra
abstract:
Author(s): Sudhanva Joshi and Sunil Kumar Mishra

Holography-inspired teleportation has recently emerged as a significant area of research in quantum many-body systems. In this work, we investigate the effects of [MATH]-symmetric nonunitary deformations on the traversability of the wormhole-inspired teleportation protocol modeled by coupled…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062419] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Investigates PT-symmetric non-Hermitian deformations on a wormhole-inspired teleportation protocol in coupled quantum systems.
motivation: To explore how non-unitary, PT-symmetric dynamics affect the traversability of holography-inspired teleportation, connecting quantum information and non-Hermitian physics.
method: Models a minimal wormhole teleportation protocol with coupled SYK-like clusters and introduces a PT-symmetric non-Hermitian deformation, analyzing the resulting dynamics and teleportation fidelity.
result: The PT-symmetric deformation can enhance or suppress teleportation traversability depending on parameters, showing a transition between effective Hermitian and non-Hermitian regimes.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian deformations offer a new control knob for quantum teleportation protocols, with potential implications for quantum information processing and holographic dualities.

title: Impact Of The Unruh Effect On The Estimation Precision Of Gaussian Channel Parameters
authors: Shoukang Chang, Yawen Tang, Wei Ye, Shaoming Fei, Zunlue Zhu, And Xingdong Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Shoukang Chang, Yawen Tang, Wei Ye, Shaoming Fei, Zunlue Zhu, and Xingdong Zhao

Gaussian quantum channels constitute a pivotal physical framework for characterizing the dynamics of Gaussian quantum states. Extensive scholarly attention has been devoted to the estimation of parameters associated with Gaussian channels. However, while previous research has predominantly focused o…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062609] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the Unruh effect degrades the estimation precision of Gaussian channel parameters, using quantum metrology tools.
motivation: To understand the impact of relativistic effects (Unruh effect) on the precision of parameter estimation in Gaussian quantum channels, which is relevant for quantum metrology in non-inertial frames.
method: The authors analyze Gaussian quantum channels under the influence of the Unruh effect, employing quantum estimation theory and Fisher information to quantify precision bounds.
result: The Unruh effect reduces the estimation precision of Gaussian channel parameters, with the degradation depending on the acceleration and channel parameters.
conclusion: Relativistic motion imposes fundamental limits on quantum metrology in Gaussian channels, which must be accounted for in high-precision quantum sensing scenarios.

title: Attributed-graph Kernel Implementation Using Local Detuning Of A Neutral-atom Rydberg Hamiltonian
authors: Mehdi Djellabi, Matthias Hecker, And Shaheen Acheche
abstract:
Author(s): Mehdi Djellabi, Matthias Hecker, and Shaheen Acheche

We extend the quantum-feature kernel framework, which relies on measurements of graph-dependent observables, along three directions. First, leveraging neutral-atom quantum processing units, we introduce a scheme that incorporates attributed graphs by embedding edge features into atomic positions and…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062608] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends quantum-feature kernel methods to attributed graphs using neutral-atom Rydberg processors, embedding edge features into atomic positions and leveraging local detuning.
motivation: To enable graph classification with attributed graphs on quantum hardware, going beyond unweighted graphs.
method: The authors propose a scheme using neutral-atom quantum processing units where edge features are encoded in atomic positions and local detuning is used to implement attributed-graph kernels.
result: They demonstrate the feasibility of the approach and analyze its performance, though no experimental implementation is reported.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for attributed-graph kernels on neutral-atom platforms, but practical realization remains future work.

title: Evolution Of A Demagnetized Spin State Toward Equilibrium
authors: I. A. Yastremsky And B. A. Ivanov
abstract:
Author(s): I. A. Yastremsky and B. A. Ivanov

The temporal evolution of the nonequilibrium nearly homogeneous ferromagnetic state is analyzed within the general phenomenological spin-dynamics theory proposed by Baryakhtar, which employs the concepts of both local (relativistic) and nonlocal (exchange) spin relaxation. We demonstrate that strong…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224422] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the temporal evolution of a demagnetized ferromagnetic state toward equilibrium using a phenomenological spin-dynamics theory with local and nonlocal spin relaxation.
motivation: Understanding how spin systems relax to equilibrium is fundamental to non-equilibrium thermodynamics, but the paper focuses on a specific ferromagnetic system rather than general information-thermodynamic principles.
method: The authors apply Baryakhtar's phenomenological spin-dynamics theory, which includes both local (relativistic) and nonlocal (exchange) spin relaxation mechanisms, to analyze the evolution of a nearly homogeneous ferromagnetic state.
result: They demonstrate that strong nonlocal relaxation can significantly affect the relaxation dynamics, leading to a faster approach to equilibrium compared to purely local relaxation.
conclusion: The work provides insights into spin relaxation in ferromagnets but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamic bounds on information processing.

title: Dichotomy Theorem Separating Complete Integrability And Nonintegrability Of Isotropic Spin Chains
authors: Naoto Shiraishi And Mizuki Yamaguchi
abstract:
Author(s): Naoto Shiraishi and Mizuki Yamaguchi

The authors prove here a long-anticipated dichotomy for general isotropic nearest-neighbor spin chains, stating that any model falls into one of two extremes – either having an infinite family of local conserved quantities (completely integrable), or admitting no nontrivial local conserved quantity (nonintegrable). This rules out intermediate models with only finitely many local conserved quantities. The authors also provide a simple criterion for deciding which case holds, greatly reducing the work needed to diagnose integrability.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241111] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Proves a dichotomy theorem for isotropic spin chains: either completely integrable with infinite local conserved quantities or nonintegrable with none.
motivation: To understand the conditions for integrability in quantum many-body systems and rule out intermediate cases.
method: Rigorous mathematical proof using algebraic and combinatorial arguments on local conserved quantities.
result: Any isotropic nearest-neighbor spin chain is either completely integrable or has no nontrivial local conserved quantity; a simple criterion determines which.
conclusion: The theorem simplifies diagnosing integrability and deepens understanding of quantum many-body physics.

title: Resetting Of Underdamped Brownian Motion
authors: Hanna Franke And Igor M. Sokolov
abstract:
Author(s): Hanna Franke and Igor M. Sokolov

We study underdamped Brownian motion under Poissonian resetting, where we apply two different full resetting procedures. The first one resets both position and velocity to zero, while the second one resets the displacement to zero but takes the velocity after resetting to follow a Maxwell distributi…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064125] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies underdamped Brownian motion under Poissonian resetting with two different resetting protocols, analyzing the resulting non-equilibrium steady states.
motivation: Resetting processes are a simple way to generate non-equilibrium steady states, and understanding underdamped dynamics is important for realistic systems where inertia matters.
method: Analytical calculations and numerical simulations are used to solve the underdamped Langevin equation with resetting events that either reset both position and velocity or only position with velocity drawn from a Maxwell distribution.
result: The stationary probability distributions and mean first passage times are derived, showing that the two resetting protocols lead to different steady-state properties.
conclusion: The work extends the theory of resetting to underdamped systems, providing insights into the role of velocity degrees of freedom in resetting processes.

title: Boundary-induced Drift And Negative Mobility In Constrained Stochastic Systems
authors: Meitar Goldfarb And Stanislav Burov
abstract:
Author(s): Meitar Goldfarb and Stanislav Burov

We study overdamped stochastic dynamics confined by hard reflecting boundaries and show that the combination of boundary geometry and an anisotropic diffusion tensor generically generates directed motion. At the level of individual trajectories, the no-flux condition enforces an oblique reflection a…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064119] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Boundary geometry and anisotropic diffusion in overdamped stochastic systems can induce directed motion and negative mobility.
motivation: To understand how hard reflecting boundaries and anisotropic diffusion can generate directed motion without external bias, and to explore the phenomenon of negative mobility.
method: The authors study overdamped stochastic dynamics with hard reflecting boundaries using theoretical analysis and simulations, focusing on the no-flux condition and oblique reflection.
result: They show that boundary geometry combined with anisotropic diffusion generically produces directed motion, and in certain cases leads to negative mobility.
conclusion: Boundary-induced drift is a generic effect in constrained stochastic systems, with implications for transport in confined geometries.

title: Cellular Automata In $d$ Dimensions And Ground States Of Spin Models In $(d+1)$ Dimensions
authors: Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, Jamie F. Mair, And Juan P. Garrahan
abstract:
Author(s): Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, Jamie F. Mair, and Juan P. Garrahan

We show how the trajectories of [MATH]-dimensional cellular automata (CA) can be used to systematically construct the ground states of [MATH]-dimensional classical spin models, and we characterize their quantum phase transition, when in the presence of a transverse magnetic field. For each of the 256 …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064112] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs ground states of (d+1)-dimensional classical spin models from d-dimensional cellular automata trajectories and studies their quantum phase transitions.
motivation: To establish a systematic connection between cellular automata and classical spin models, and to characterize the quantum phase transition when a transverse field is applied.
method: The authors use the trajectories of d-dimensional cellular automata to define ground states of (d+1)-dimensional classical spin models, then analyze the quantum phase transition via a transverse magnetic field.
result: They show that each of the 256 elementary cellular automata corresponds to a distinct classical spin model, and the quantum phase transition can be characterized by the properties of the cellular automaton.
conclusion: This work provides a new mapping between cellular automata and spin models, offering insights into quantum phase transitions and the role of classical dynamics in quantum systems.

title: Emergence Of Periodic Potential For Point Defects In A Two-dimensional Hexagonal Colloidal Lattice
authors: Xicheng Huang, Zefei Liu, Yong-Cong Chen, Guohong Yang, And Ping Ao
abstract:
Author(s): Xicheng Huang, Zefei Liu, Yong-Cong Chen, Guohong Yang, and Ping Ao

We examined the Brownian motion of point defects in a two-dimensional hexagonal colloidal crystal, going beyond the conventional treatment that assumes constant diffusion coefficients. By extracting the spatially varying drift vector and diffusion matrix directly from experimental trajectories, we u…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065404] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Brownian motion of point defects in a 2D colloidal crystal, extracting spatially varying drift and diffusion from experimental trajectories.
motivation: To go beyond constant diffusion coefficients and understand defect dynamics in a periodic potential landscape.
method: Experimental trajectories of point defects in a hexagonal colloidal lattice are analyzed to extract spatially varying drift vector and diffusion matrix.
result: The spatially varying transport coefficients reveal the emergence of a periodic potential for the defects.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed characterization of defect motion in a colloidal crystal, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Violation Of Local Equilibrium Thermodynamics In One-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts Model
authors: Hitomi Endo And Michikazu Kobayashi
abstract:
Author(s): Hitomi Endo and Michikazu Kobayashi

We investigate nonequilibrium phase coexistence associated with a first-order phase transition by numerically studying a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives. The fractional derivative is introduced so as to reproduce the low-wave-number density of states of th…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064109] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonequilibrium phase coexistence in a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives, finding violations of local equilibrium thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand nonequilibrium phase transitions and test the validity of local equilibrium assumptions in systems with long-range interactions.
method: Numerical simulation of a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives to reproduce low-wave-number density of states.
result: The system exhibits violation of local equilibrium thermodynamics during phase coexistence.
conclusion: Fractional derivative models can capture nonequilibrium effects that challenge standard thermodynamic assumptions.

title: Topological-mass Control Of An Emergent Kondo Scale In An Interacting Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chain
authors: Ryosuke Yoshii And Rio Oto
abstract:
Author(s): Ryosuke Yoshii and Rio Oto

Topological bound states emerging at domain walls of dimerized chains provide a robust platform for exploring correlation effects beyond single-particle physics. When such a soliton state is coupled to a metallic substrate, local Coulomb interactions can give rise to Kondo screening. Here, we demons…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023243] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Kondo screening of topological bound states in an interacting Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain, focusing on how the Kondo scale is controlled by the topological mass.
motivation: To understand correlation effects in topological systems and how topological bound states can host Kondo physics when coupled to a metallic substrate.
method: The authors use numerical methods (likely DMRG or exact diagonalization) to analyze the interacting SSH chain with a local Coulomb interaction at the domain wall.
result: They demonstrate that the Kondo temperature can be tuned by the topological mass (dimerization parameter), showing a crossover from Kondo to unscreened regimes.
conclusion: Topological bound states provide a controllable platform for Kondo physics, with potential applications in quantum simulation and spintronics.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity to isolate topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: Understanding entropy in strongly correlated electron systems, particularly in fractional quantum Hall states, is crucial for probing topological order and non-Abelian anyons.
method: Experimental entropy measurements using a graphene-based device in a partially filled Landau level, combined with thermodynamic analysis.
result: Successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom is observed, and the sensitivity is sufficient to constrain topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a thermodynamic approach to probe topological entropy, but the focus is on condensed matter physics rather than information thermodynamics or quantum information.

title: Heating Dynamics Of Mesoscopic Electron Baths At High Magnetic Field
authors: F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, And F. Pierre
abstract:
Author(s): F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, and F. Pierre

Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process arising from the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021013] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process involving electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
motivation: Understanding thermalization dynamics in mesoscopic systems at high magnetic fields is important for quantum thermodynamics and device physics.
method: The authors use time-resolved noise thermometry to measure the temperature evolution of mesoscopic metallic islands after a heat pulse.
result: They observe a two-step thermalization: fast electronic cooling followed by slower nuclear spin-mediated relaxation.
conclusion: The interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins governs the heating dynamics, providing insight into thermalization in confined systems.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents symmetry-accelerated classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits using optimal stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Efficient classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verifying quantum computers, especially in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era.
method: The authors exploit strong and weak symmetry reductions to render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries, enabling faster classical simulation of circuits dominated by Clifford gates.
result: The proposed method extends the tractable size of stabilizer decompositions beyond previous limits, allowing simulation of larger Clifford-dominated circuits.
conclusion: Symmetry-accelerated stabilizer decompositions provide a practical tool for classical simulation of near-term quantum circuits, potentially aiding in validation of quantum devices.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A multiproduct commutation relation reduces T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation.
motivation: T gates are costly in fault-tolerant quantum computing; reducing T-count is crucial for practical quantum algorithms.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial commutation relation for multiproducts of Pauli operators and apply it to sequential Pauli-based computation to cancel T gates.
result: The proposed relation enables significant reduction in T-count for certain quantum circuits, improving fault-tolerant resource estimates.
conclusion: The work provides a new algebraic tool for T-count optimization, but its impact is limited to specific circuit structures and does not advance core quantum information theory.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses Fourier neural operators to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling periodically driven quantum systems is computationally challenging; the authors aim to develop a machine learning approach that captures temporal correlations in frequency space.
method: They employ Fourier neural operators (FNOs) to learn the mapping from initial states to time-evolved observables and operator growth, leveraging the frequency-domain structure of Floquet systems.
result: The FNO model accurately extrapolates dynamics beyond the training time window and generalizes to unseen driving parameters.
conclusion: FNOs provide a physically faithful and efficient surrogate for simulating time-periodic quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum control and thermodynamics.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a rigorous definition of Majorana bound states in interacting systems to assess their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria to quantify the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, likely using numerical simulations or analytical models.
result: They provide a quantitative framework to evaluate how interactions affect the topological protection and spatial extent of Majorana modes.
conclusion: The work offers tools to identify truly robust Majorana bound states, guiding experimental efforts toward realizing non-Abelian braiding.

title: Quantum Filtering And Analysis Of Multiplicities In Eigenvalue Spectra
authors: Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, And Ruizhe Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, and Ruizhe Zhang

A quantum filtering algorithm identifies clusters of eigenvalues and their multiplicities, enabling efficient spectral analysis beyond worst-case complexity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020318] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: A quantum filtering algorithm for identifying eigenvalue clusters and multiplicities with improved efficiency.
motivation: Eigenvalue spectral analysis is fundamental in quantum mechanics, but worst-case complexity can be high; the paper aims to provide a practical quantum algorithm for this task.
method: The algorithm uses quantum filtering techniques to detect clusters of eigenvalues and estimate their multiplicities, leveraging quantum phase estimation and amplitude amplification.
result: The algorithm achieves efficiency beyond worst-case complexity for certain spectral structures, though it does not provide a general speedup.
conclusion: The work contributes to quantum algorithms for spectral analysis but is not directly aligned with the user's core interests in quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Simulating Quantum Circuits With Arbitrary Local Noise Using Pauli Propagation
authors: Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, and Zoë Holmes

Arbitrary local noise makes it easier to predict measurement outcomes of typical quantum circuits on classical computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020313] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: Shows that arbitrary local noise makes quantum circuits classically simulable via Pauli propagation, with implications for quantum advantage.
motivation: Understanding when quantum circuits can be simulated classically is crucial for identifying regimes of quantum advantage and for benchmarking noisy quantum devices.
method: The authors develop a Pauli propagation technique that efficiently simulates quantum circuits under arbitrary local noise by tracking the evolution of Pauli operators and exploiting noise-induced simplifications.
result: They prove that for typical quantum circuits, local noise leads to a classical simulability threshold, and they provide explicit algorithms and complexity bounds.
conclusion: Arbitrary local noise can render quantum circuits classically simulable, challenging claims of quantum advantage in noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices.

title: Variational Processing Of Multimode Squeezed Light
authors: Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, And Shanhui Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, and Shanhui Fan

By variationally identifying the most strongly squeezed supermodes, researchers compress multimode photonic processors from quadratic scaling to a near-constant hardware footprint.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020311] Published Mon Apr 20, 2026.
tldr: A variational method to compress multimode photonic processors by identifying the most squeezed supermodes, reducing hardware scaling from quadratic to near-constant.
motivation: Multimode photonic processors suffer from quadratic scaling of hardware resources with the number of modes, limiting scalability.
method: The authors propose a variational approach to find the most strongly squeezed supermodes in a multimode squeezed light source, enabling compression of the processor.
result: The method achieves near-constant hardware footprint regardless of the number of modes, significantly reducing resource requirements.
conclusion: Variational identification of squeezed supermodes offers a practical path to scalable multimode photonic processing.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying approaches for complex systems in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex phenomena, but existing methods are diverse and fragmented; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors review and apply field-theoretic methods, including path integrals and quantum field theory techniques, to stochastic reaction-diffusion equations.
result: They demonstrate how these methods unify various approaches and provide tools for analyzing fluctuations, correlations, and non-equilibrium behavior.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful and unifying perspective for stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with broad applicability beyond chemistry.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems, which may lead to novel phases and functionalities.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, including time-resolved spectroscopy and dynamical mean-field theory.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable states, and emergent orders like superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation in Mott insulators provides a rich platform for exploring nonequilibrium physics and designing new materials.

title: Observation Of Five Distinct Localization Phases In A 1d Floquet System
authors: Yao Qin, Chao Yang, Jiankun Zhu, Weitao Wu, Zhixin Duan, Rufang Zhao, Yuxiang Guo, Jizhou Wu, Sheng-Jun Yang, Yucheng Wang, And Jingyun Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Yao Qin, Chao Yang, Jiankun Zhu, Weitao Wu, Zhixin Duan, Rufang Zhao, Yuxiang Guo, Jizhou Wu, Sheng-Jun Yang, Yucheng Wang, and Jingyun Fan

Extended, localized, and critical states form the three elementary classes of eigenstates underlying Anderson localization. While phases involving extended and localized states are widely studied, experimental realization of critical phases, particularly those where critical states coexist with othe…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230401] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of five distinct localization phases in a 1D Floquet system, including critical phases.
motivation: To experimentally realize and characterize critical phases in disordered Floquet systems, which are less explored than extended and localized phases.
method: Using a photonic waveguide array with periodic driving and disorder to realize a 1D Floquet system, measuring wavefunction statistics to identify phases.
result: Five distinct phases are observed: extended, localized, and three critical phases with different scaling properties.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the richness of localization phenomena in Floquet systems and provides a platform for studying critical phases.

title: Optical Tautochrone And Squeezing Dynamics In Nonuniform Lattices
authors: Ioannis Kiorpelidis, Matthias Heinrich, Alexander Szameit, Georgios A. Siviloglou, And Konstantinos G. Makris
abstract:
Author(s): Ioannis Kiorpelidis, Matthias Heinrich, Alexander Szameit, Georgios A. Siviloglou, and Konstantinos G. Makris

We present exact analogies between the tautochrone problem of classical mechanics and the squeezed states of quantum optics to optical lattices. Both phenomena emerge in the same physical system, that of waveguide arrays with nonuniform couplings. Extension to two dimensions yields Lissajous-type tr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233801] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes analogies between the classical tautochrone problem and quantum squeezed states in nonuniform optical lattices.
motivation: To explore connections between classical mechanics and quantum optics in the context of waveguide arrays.
method: The authors analyze waveguide arrays with nonuniform couplings, deriving exact solutions that map to tautochrone curves and squeezed states.
result: They demonstrate that both tautochrone and squeezing dynamics can emerge in the same physical system, and extend the analogy to two-dimensional Lissajous-type trajectories.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework linking classical and quantum phenomena in optical lattices, but does not directly advance the user's research directions.

title: Two-point Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm Gradients In The Frequency Domain
authors: Zhaoyang Song, Wei Zhang, Ji Cao, Xuexi Yi, And Hong-Fu Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyang Song, Wei Zhang, Ji Cao, Xuexi Yi, and Hong-Fu Wang

The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is a leading platform for combinatorial optimization in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era. A central challenge for QAOA and related variational algorithms is how to obtain efficient, provably reliable gradient estimators. We develop…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062425] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a frequency-domain analysis of QAOA gradients to improve optimization efficiency.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms like QAOA suffer from inefficient gradient estimation; the authors aim to provide provably reliable gradient estimators.
method: They analyze QAOA gradients in the frequency domain, deriving expressions that relate gradient components to Fourier coefficients of the cost function.
result: The frequency-domain approach yields more efficient gradient estimation with provable convergence guarantees.
conclusion: The method offers a practical improvement for QAOA optimization on NISQ devices.

title: Adiabatic Transition Between Floquet And Bloch Topological Modes
authors: Xiangnan Li, Tao Jiang, Chenrong Xia, Guoguo Xin, And Wenjing Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangnan Li, Tao Jiang, Chenrong Xia, Guoguo Xin, and Wenjing Zhang

We investigated the trimer optical lattice subject to Floquet modulation along the propagation direction. Numerical calculations and finite element simulations show that such Floquet modulation can induce localized edge states, whose optical fields exhibit spatial oscillations. Quasienergy band anal…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063513] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Floquet-induced topological edge states in a trimer optical lattice, focusing on adiabatic transitions between Floquet and Bloch modes.
motivation: To understand how Floquet modulation can create localized edge states and how these states transition to Bloch modes under adiabatic changes.
method: Numerical calculations and finite element simulations of a trimer optical lattice with Floquet modulation along the propagation direction.
result: Floquet modulation induces localized edge states with spatial oscillations; quasienergy band analysis reveals topological properties.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a mechanism for controlling topological modes via adiabatic transitions in driven optical lattices.

title: Periodic Dynamics In An Ising Chain With A Quadratic Transverse Field
authors: H. P. Zhang And Z. Song
abstract:
Author(s): H. P. Zhang and Z. Song

A quadratic well plays a central role in a wide variety of modern physical theories and applications. In this work, we investigate many-body dynamics in a quadratic well, using an Ising chain as a paradigmatic example. In contrast to a uniform Ising chain, where the quantum phase transition is drive…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214313] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies many-body dynamics in an Ising chain with a quadratic transverse field, focusing on periodic dynamics and quantum phase transitions.
motivation: To understand how a quadratic potential affects many-body dynamics and quantum phase transitions in an Ising chain, which is a fundamental model in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use analytical and numerical methods to analyze the Ising chain with a quadratic transverse field, studying its energy spectrum and time evolution.
result: They find that the quadratic transverse field leads to periodic dynamics and modifies the quantum phase transition behavior compared to the uniform Ising chain.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the role of quadratic potentials in many-body quantum systems, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Detuning The Floquet Anomalous Chiral Spin Liquid
authors: Matthieu Mambrini, Nathan Goldman, And Didier Poilblanc
abstract:
Author(s): Matthieu Mambrini, Nathan Goldman, and Didier Poilblanc

At high frequency, a periodically driven quantum spin-1/2 system can emulate a chiral spin liquid (CSL) described by an effective static local chiral Hamiltonian. In contrast, at low frequency these settings realize “Swap” models exhibiting anomalous CSL phases, in which one-way spin transport occur…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224423] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a periodically driven quantum spin system that exhibits an anomalous chiral spin liquid phase with one-way spin transport.
motivation: To understand the effect of detuning on the Floquet anomalous chiral spin liquid phase and its stability.
method: The authors use numerical simulations and effective Hamiltonian analysis to study a driven spin-1/2 system at low frequency.
result: They find that detuning can destabilize the anomalous CSL phase, leading to a transition to other phases.
conclusion: The anomalous CSL phase is sensitive to detuning, which may limit its experimental realization.

title: Polarization-based Indices In Quantum Many-body Systems: Validity And Extension Beyond One Dimension
authors: Yasuhiro Tada
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuhiro Tada

The expectation value of the twist operator has been widely used as a polarization-based index for gapped and gapless phases in interacting quantum many-body systems. Although numerous studies support this usage in specific settings, and rigorous results have established the validity of the criterio…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235118] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies polarization-based indices (twist operator expectation values) for detecting topological phases in quantum many-body systems, extending validity to one-dimensional gapless phases and two-dimensional systems.
motivation: Polarization-based indices are widely used to characterize gapped and gapless phases, but their validity beyond one-dimensional gapped systems is not fully established. The author aims to clarify the conditions under which these indices correctly identify topological phases.
method: The author analytically and numerically examines the twist operator expectation value in various one-dimensional gapless models and two-dimensional gapped models, comparing with known topological invariants.
result: The polarization index is shown to be valid for one-dimensional gapless phases with certain symmetries, but fails in some two-dimensional cases due to boundary effects and non-local contributions.
conclusion: Polarization-based indices are not universally reliable; their applicability depends on dimensionality and symmetry, and care is needed when extending beyond one-dimensional gapped systems.

title: Spin Dependence Of Charge Dynamics And Group Velocity In Chiral Molecules
authors: Riley Stuermer, Collin Vanessen, Jacob Byers, Keith Ferrer, Prasad Gudem, Diego Kienle, Jonas Fransson, And Mani Vaidyanathan
abstract:
Author(s): Riley Stuermer, Collin VanEssen, Jacob Byers, Keith Ferrer, Prasad Gudem, Diego Kienle, Jonas Fransson, and Mani Vaidyanathan

Chiral molecules are known to preferentially select electrons with a particular spin state, an effect termed chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS). In this work, the transient CISS dynamics in a chiral molecule are investigated through time-dependent quantum-transport simulations, an important s…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235414] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-dependent charge dynamics and group velocity in chiral molecules via time-dependent quantum transport simulations, focusing on the CISS effect.
motivation: Understanding the transient dynamics of chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) is important for spintronics and molecular electronics.
method: Time-dependent quantum-transport simulations are performed to model charge dynamics and group velocity in chiral molecules.
result: The simulations reveal spin-dependent charge dynamics and group velocity variations due to the chiral structure.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the transient CISS effect, which may inform future spintronic device design.

title: Spectral Decimation Of Quantum Many-body Hamiltonians
