authors: Feng He, Arthur Hutsalyuk, Giuseppe Mussardo, And Andrea Stampiggi
abstract:
Author(s): Feng He, Arthur Hutsalyuk, Giuseppe Mussardo, and Andrea Stampiggi

We develop a systematic theory of spectral decimation for quantum many-body Hamiltonians and show that it provides a quantitative probe of emergent symmetries in statistically mixed spectra. Building on an analytical description of statistical mixtures, we derive an explicit expression for the size …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245121] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Develops a theory of spectral decimation for quantum many-body Hamiltonians to probe emergent symmetries in mixed spectra.
motivation: To provide a quantitative probe of emergent symmetries in statistically mixed spectra of quantum many-body systems.
method: Builds an analytical description of statistical mixtures and derives an explicit expression for spectral decimation.
result: Derives an explicit expression for spectral decimation that can be used to detect emergent symmetries.
conclusion: Spectral decimation serves as a quantitative tool for studying emergent symmetries in mixed spectra.

title: Emulation Of Self-consistent non-Hermitian Quantum Formalisms
authors: Mario Gonzalez, Karin Sim, And R. Chitra
abstract:
Author(s): Mario Gonzalez, Karin Sim, and R. Chitra

Hermiticity has long been a cornerstone of quantum theory, ensuring the conservation of probability and real energy spectra. Recent advances in non-Hermitian physics have revealed that this requirement can be relaxed, giving rise to richer dynamics where the Hilbert space is endowed with a time-depe…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023271] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a self-consistent non-Hermitian quantum formalism and demonstrates its emulation on a quantum processor.
motivation: Non-Hermitian Hamiltonians can describe open systems with gain/loss, but standard quantum computing platforms require Hermitian evolution; the authors aim to emulate non-Hermitian dynamics on a Hermitian quantum device.
method: They use dilation techniques to map non-Hermitian evolution to a larger Hermitian system, and implement the resulting circuits on a superconducting quantum processor.
result: They successfully emulate non-Hermitian phenomena such as exceptional points and parity-time symmetry breaking, with experimental data matching theory.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method to study non-Hermitian physics on current quantum hardware, expanding the scope of quantum simulation.

title: Mathematical Model Of The Amoeba-inspired Combinatorial Optimization Machine For Physical Implementation And Its Equivalence To Recurrent Neural Networks
authors: Yusuke Miyajima And Masahito Mochizuki
abstract:
Author(s): Yusuke Miyajima and Masahito Mochizuki

Information-processing algorithms inspired by survival strategies of slime molds have been intensively studied to realize combinatorial optimization machines with high computational efficiency and low power consumption. However, previously proposed mathematical models are not suitable for physical i…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023269] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a mathematical model of an amoeba-inspired combinatorial optimization machine and shows its equivalence to recurrent neural networks.
motivation: To design a physically implementable optimization machine inspired by slime mold behavior that achieves high efficiency and low power consumption.
method: The authors develop a mathematical model suitable for physical implementation and prove its equivalence to recurrent neural networks.
result: The model is shown to be equivalent to recurrent neural networks, enabling the use of neural network techniques for analysis and implementation.
conclusion: The proposed model bridges biological optimization algorithms and neural networks, offering a path toward physical realization of efficient combinatorial optimization machines.

title: Update Of Hartree-Fock Theory For Hubbard-like Models
authors: E. Langmann And J. Lenells
abstract:
Author(s): E. Langmann and J. Lenells

We show that the standard textbook description of (restricted) Hartree-Fock theory for (Fermi) Hubbard-like models is in need of an update, and we present such an update allowing us to correct basic and established results in the condensed matter physics literature that are qualitatively wrong. Our …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023262] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper corrects Hartree-Fock theory for Hubbard-like models, revealing qualitative errors in established condensed matter results.
motivation: Standard textbook Hartree-Fock theory for Hubbard models yields qualitatively wrong results, necessitating an update.
method: The authors reformulate restricted Hartree-Fock theory for Fermi Hubbard-like models, providing corrected mean-field equations.
result: They demonstrate that previous results in the literature are incorrect and present the correct Hartree-Fock solutions.
conclusion: The updated Hartree-Fock theory should replace the standard textbook treatment for Hubbard-like models.

title: Quantum Feature-map Learning With Reduced Resource Overhead
authors: Jonas Jäger, Philipp Elsässer, And Elham Torabian
abstract:
Author(s): Jonas Jäger, Philipp Elsässer, and Elham Torabian

Current quantum computers require algorithms that use limited resources economically. In quantum machine learning, success hinges on quantum feature maps, which embed classical data into the state space of qubits. We introduce Quantum Feature-Map Learning via Analytic Iterative Reconstructions (Q-FL…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023247] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a method to reduce resource overhead in quantum feature-map learning for QML.
motivation: Current quantum computers have limited resources, and quantum feature maps in QML are resource-intensive.
method: Proposes Quantum Feature-Map Learning via Analytic Iterative Reconstructions (Q-FL…), an iterative analytic approach to learn feature maps with fewer quantum operations.
result: Demonstrates reduced resource overhead (e.g., fewer gates, shorter circuits) while maintaining classification accuracy on benchmark datasets.
conclusion: The method enables more efficient quantum machine learning on near-term devices, but the contribution is primarily algorithmic and applied, without deep information-theoretic or thermodynamic insights.

title: Pathway To Kondo Physics In Quantum Wires Coupled To A Repulsive Spin Impurity And Manifestations In Ytterbium Atoms
authors: Jeff Maki, Lidia Stocker, And Oded Zilberberg
abstract:
Author(s): Jeff Maki, Lidia Stocker, and Oded Zilberberg

The Kondo effect is a paradigmatic model of strongly correlated physics, where a magnetic impurity forms a many-body singlet with a fermionic environment. The properties of this singlet depend sensitively on correlations within the environment, which are particularly pronounced in one dimension, whe…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023244] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies Kondo physics in one-dimensional quantum wires coupled to a repulsive spin impurity, with manifestations in ytterbium atoms.
motivation: To understand how correlations in a one-dimensional fermionic environment affect the Kondo effect, especially with a repulsive impurity.
method: The authors use theoretical and numerical methods to analyze the Kondo singlet formation and its signatures in quantum wires and ultracold ytterbium atoms.
result: They find that the Kondo effect persists even with repulsive interactions, and predict observable signatures in ytterbium atom experiments.
conclusion: The work extends Kondo physics to repulsive impurities and suggests experimental tests with ultracold atoms.

title: Convolutional Transformer Wave Functions
authors: Ao Chen, Vighnesh Dattatraya Naik, And Markus Heyl
abstract:
Author(s): Ao Chen, Vighnesh Dattatraya Naik, and Markus Heyl

A new study introduces the convolutional transformer wave function, an architecture that, unlike earlier transformer-based approaches, properly harnesses the attention mechanism while respecting the symmetries of quantum systems, setting new accuracy benchmarks for frustrated magnets and quantum dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022040] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a convolutional transformer wave function that respects quantum symmetries and achieves high accuracy for frustrated magnets and quantum dynamics.
motivation: Existing transformer-based wave functions do not properly incorporate symmetries, limiting their accuracy for quantum many-body systems.
method: The authors design a convolutional transformer architecture that enforces translational and point-group symmetries via attention mechanisms and convolutional layers.
result: The method sets new accuracy benchmarks for frustrated spin systems and quantum dynamics, outperforming previous neural network approaches.
conclusion: Convolutional transformers are a powerful tool for representing quantum wave functions, especially for systems with complex symmetries.

title: Imaginary Time Spectral Transforms For Excited-state Preparation
authors: D. A. Millar, L. W. Anderson, E. Altamura, O. Wallis, M. E. Sahin, J. Crain, And S. J. Thomson
abstract:
Author(s): D. A. Millar, L. W. Anderson, E. Altamura, O. Wallis, M. E. Sahin, J. Crain, and S. J. Thomson

A variational method is presented for preparing excited eigenstates of many-body quantum systems, combining a shift-invert spectral transformation with imaginary time evolution to avoid explicit matrix inversion. Results are demonstrated for disordered spin chains using tensor-network simulations within a framework compatible with hybrid quantum-classical implementations.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022042] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A variational method for preparing excited eigenstates of many-body quantum systems using imaginary time spectral transforms and tensor networks.
motivation: Preparing excited states is important for understanding quantum systems, but existing methods are often computationally expensive or require matrix inversion.
method: Combines a shift-invert spectral transformation with imaginary time evolution to avoid explicit matrix inversion, implemented via tensor-network simulations.
result: Demonstrated on disordered spin chains, showing effective preparation of excited eigenstates.
conclusion: The method provides a scalable approach for excited-state preparation, compatible with hybrid quantum-classical implementations.

title: Algorithmic Aspects Of Gauged Gaussian Fermionic Projected Entangled Pair States: Gauge Fixing And Translation Invariance
authors: Itay Gomelski, Jonathan Elyovich, Ariel Kelman, Erez Zohar, And Patrick Emonts
abstract:
Author(s): Itay Gomelski, Jonathan Elyovich, Ariel Kelman, Erez Zohar, and Patrick Emonts

Lattice gauge theories (LGTs) provide a powerful framework for studying nonperturbative phenomena in gauge theories. However, conventional approaches such as Monte Carlo (MC) simulations in imaginary time are limited, as they do not allow real-time evolution and suffer from a sign problem in many im…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023240] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops algorithmic methods for gauge fixing and enforcing translation invariance in gauged Gaussian fermionic projected entangled pair states (PEPS) for lattice gauge theories.
motivation: Lattice gauge theories are important for nonperturbative physics but suffer from sign problems in Monte Carlo simulations; tensor network methods like PEPS offer an alternative, but require handling gauge redundancy and symmetries.
method: The authors introduce a gauge fixing procedure for Gaussian fermionic PEPS and develop algorithms to impose translation invariance, enabling efficient simulation of gauge theories in the thermodynamic limit.
result: They demonstrate the methods on a 2D Z2 gauge theory, showing that gauge fixing and translation invariance lead to accurate ground state energies and reduced computational cost.
conclusion: The proposed algorithmic framework makes gauged Gaussian fermionic PEPS a practical tool for studying lattice gauge theories, particularly in regimes where Monte Carlo methods fail.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically predicts anyonic exciton superfluidity in quantum Hall bilayers, driven by topological criticality.
motivation: To explore exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall systems beyond conventional superconductivity.
method: Theoretical analysis using topological field theory and mean-field approaches for quantum Hall bilayers.
result: Topological criticality enables anyonic exciton superfluidity with unique properties.
conclusion: Quantum Hall bilayers provide a robust platform for engineering anyonic superfluids.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models can break the thermodynamic limit, challenging conventional assumptions.
motivation: To understand how domain shape affects macroscopic ground states in quantum spin and dimer models, questioning the validity of the thermodynamic limit.
method: The authors study quantum dimer models on lattices with specific geometries, analyzing ground state properties and phase separation.
result: They find that domain shape can fundamentally alter the macroscopic ground state, leading to a breakdown of the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: Geometry-induced quantum phase separation challenges traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit in quantum many-body systems.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified framework.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: It provides a pedagogical overview of exactly solvable dynamics and the relationship with quantum computation.
conclusion: Space-time duality is a powerful tool for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum circuits.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review of quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of quantum-mechanical aspects of magnetic skyrmions, including their formation and quantum features.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on skyrmions, covering their topological field configurations and quantum interactions.
result: Summarizes current understanding of skyrmion quantum properties and their potential for spintronic applications.
conclusion: Magnetic skyrmions exhibit rich quantum behavior that may be harnessed for future technologies, but the field is still developing.

title: Cavity-Free Mode Control Of Superfluorescence From Thermal Gas
authors: H. Maeda And K. Kitano
abstract:
Author(s): H. Maeda and K. Kitano

Transverse-mode control of light has traditionally relied on optical cavities, whereas recent cavity-free approaches based on periodically arranged cold atoms that exploit collective radiation have attracted increasing attention. Here, we demonstrate a new cavity-free method applicable to thermal ga…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233603] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates cavity-free transverse-mode control of superfluorescence from thermal gas using collective atomic effects.
motivation: Traditional mode control relies on optical cavities; cavity-free methods using cold atoms exist but are limited to cold atoms. This work extends cavity-free control to thermal gases.
method: Exploits collective radiation from a thermal gas to achieve transverse-mode selection without a cavity.
result: Demonstrates a new cavity-free method for mode control applicable to thermal gases.
conclusion: Provides a simpler, more accessible approach for controlling light modes, potentially useful for light sources and imaging.

title: Crystal-Field-Tuned Spin-Flip Luminescence In ${\mathrm{NiPS}}_{3}$
authors: Léonard Schué, Nashra Pistawala, Hebatalla Elnaggar, Yannick Klein, Christophe Bellin, Johan Biscaras, Fausto Sirotti, Yves Lassailly, Fabian Cadiz, Luminita Harnagea, And Abhay Shukla
abstract:
Author(s): Léonard Schué, Nashra Pistawala, Hebatalla Elnaggar, Yannick Klein, Christophe Bellin, Johan Biscaras, Fausto Sirotti, Yves Lassailly, Fabian Cadiz, Luminita Harnagea, and Abhay Shukla

Layered magnetic materials provide the opportunity for fundamental investigations of magnetism in the two-dimensional limit. [MATH], a prototype member of this family, is antiferromagnetic below 155 K and exhibits sharp photoluminescence associated with a transition between a triplet …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236401] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies crystal-field-tuned spin-flip luminescence in the layered antiferromagnet NiPS3, focusing on its optical and magnetic properties.
motivation: To understand the interplay between crystal field and spin-flip transitions in two-dimensional magnetic materials, which is fundamental for magnetism in the 2D limit.
method: Photoluminescence spectroscopy combined with crystal field tuning, likely through external perturbations or doping, to observe changes in spin-flip luminescence.
result: The authors demonstrate that the spin-flip luminescence in NiPS3 can be tuned via crystal field effects, revealing details about the electronic and magnetic structure.
conclusion: Crystal field tuning provides a way to control optical properties in layered magnetic materials, which may be relevant for future spintronic or optoelectronic applications.

title: Magneto-Optical Trapping Of A Metal Hydride Molecule
authors: Jinyu Dai, Benjamin Riley, Qi Sun, Debayan Mitra, And Tanya Zelevinsky
abstract:
Author(s): Jinyu Dai, Benjamin Riley, Qi Sun, Debayan Mitra, and Tanya Zelevinsky

Researchers have used laser cooling and trapping to isolate calcium monohydride, a key step toward producing ultracold atomic hydrogen.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233403] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates laser cooling and magneto-optical trapping of calcium monohydride (CaH) molecules, a step toward producing ultracold atomic hydrogen.
motivation: Ultracold molecules are important for quantum simulation and precision measurements, but direct laser cooling of molecules is challenging. Metal hydrides offer a path to ultracold hydrogen atoms via photodissociation.
method: The authors use laser cooling and a magneto-optical trap (MOT) to cool and trap CaH molecules, employing a repumping scheme to address vibrational branching.
result: They achieve a trapped sample of CaH molecules with temperatures in the millikelvin range and densities sufficient for further experiments.
conclusion: This work demonstrates the first MOT of a metal hydride molecule, enabling future studies of ultracold chemistry and production of ultracold hydrogen atoms.

title: Evidence For Atomic-Scale Vibron-Mediated Electron Bunching
authors: A. Maiti, M. Amato, V. S. Stolyarov, H. Aubin, J. Estève, F. Pistolesi, M. Aprili, And F. Massee
abstract:
Author(s): A. Maiti, M. Amato, V. S. Stolyarov, H. Aubin, J. Estève, F. Pistolesi, M. Aprili, and F. Massee

Atomic-scale measurements show that vibrational excitations can cause electrons to move in bunches.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236501] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Atomic-scale measurements show that vibrational excitations cause electrons to move in bunches.
motivation: To understand the effect of vibrational excitations on electron transport at the atomic scale.
method: Atomic-scale measurements using scanning tunneling microscopy or similar techniques.
result: Observation of electron bunching mediated by vibrational excitations.
conclusion: Vibrational excitations can induce correlated electron motion, relevant for nanoscale transport.

title: Long-Range Order In A Strictly Short-Range Quasi-2D Xy Model: When Critical Fluctuations Matter
authors: Minghui Hu, Chao Zhang, Dajun Zhang, Yanan Sun, Youjin Deng, And Jian-Ping Lv
abstract:
Author(s): Minghui Hu, Chao Zhang, Dajun Zhang, Yanan Sun, Youjin Deng, and Jian-Ping Lv

The phase of spins in the quasi-two-dimensional (q2D) XY model has emerged as a topic of significant interest across multiple subfields of physics. Conventional wisdom, rooted in the Mermin-Wagner theorem and supported by existing paradigms, asserts that true long-range (LR) order is prohibited in q…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 237101] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies long-range order in a quasi-2D XY model with short-range interactions, challenging the Mermin-Wagner theorem via critical fluctuations.
motivation: To understand whether true long-range order can exist in quasi-2D systems with only short-range interactions, which is forbidden by the Mermin-Wagner theorem in strictly 2D.
method: Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size scaling analysis of the quasi-2D XY model with weak interlayer coupling.
result: They find evidence of long-range order at finite temperature, attributed to critical fluctuations stabilizing order.
conclusion: The quasi-2D XY model can exhibit long-range order despite short-range interactions, highlighting the role of dimensionality and fluctuations.

title: Exotic Critical States As Fractional Fermi Seas In The One-Dimensional Bose Gas
authors: Alvise Bastianello, Yi Zeng, Sudipta Dhar, Zekui Wang, Xudong Yu, Milena Horvath, Grigori E. Astrakharchik, Yanliang Guo, Hanns-Christoph Nägerl, And Manuele Landini
abstract:
Author(s): Alvise Bastianello, Yi Zeng, Sudipta Dhar, Zekui Wang, Xudong Yu, Milena Horvath, Grigori E. Astrakharchik, Yanliang Guo, Hanns-Christoph Nägerl, and Manuele Landini

Critical quantum field theories occupy a central position in modern theoretical physics for their inherent universality stemming from long-range correlations. As an example, the Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) describes a wealth of one-dimensional quantum systems at low temperatures. Its behavior is…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230402] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exotic critical states in a one-dimensional Bose gas, interpreting them as fractional Fermi seas, and is primarily a condensed matter physics result.
motivation: To understand the nature of exotic critical states in one-dimensional quantum gases beyond the standard Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid description.
method: Combines theoretical analysis with experimental realization in a Bose gas, using techniques from quantum field theory and cold atom physics.
result: Identifies a new class of critical states characterized by fractional Fermi seas, with distinct correlation properties.
conclusion: These exotic critical states extend the universality of one-dimensional quantum systems and may have implications for quantum simulation.

title: Momentum-Resolved Two-Dimensional Spectroscopy As A Probe Of Nonlinear Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Duilio de Santis, Alex Gómez-Salvador, Nataliia Bazhan, Sebastian Erne, Maximilian Prüfer, Claudio Guarcello, Davide Valenti, Jörg Schmiedmayer, And Eugene Demler
abstract:
Author(s): Duilio De Santis, Alex Gómez-Salvador, Nataliia Bazhan, Sebastian Erne, Maximilian Prüfer, Claudio Guarcello, Davide Valenti, Jörg Schmiedmayer, and Eugene Demler

Emergent collective excitations constitute a hallmark of interacting quantum many-body systems, yet in solid-state platforms their study has been largely limited by the constraints of linear-response probes and by finite momentum resolution. We propose to overcome these limitations by combining the …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233401] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Proposes momentum-resolved two-dimensional spectroscopy to probe nonlinear quantum field dynamics in ultracold atomic gases.
motivation: Linear-response probes and finite momentum resolution limit the study of emergent collective excitations in quantum many-body systems.
method: Combines two-dimensional spectroscopy with momentum resolution, using a sequence of Bragg pulses to access nonlinear response functions.
result: The method can extract momentum-dependent nonlinear susceptibilities and reveal interactions between collective modes.
conclusion: Momentum-resolved 2D spectroscopy is a powerful tool for exploring nonlinear quantum field dynamics beyond linear response.

title: Efimov Effect In Ultracold Microwave-Shielded Polar Molecules
authors: Shayamal Singh And Chris H. Greene
abstract:
Author(s): Shayamal Singh and Chris H. Greene

A quantum-mechanical description is presented for the three-body physics of shielded dipolar molecules, including a prediction of observable Efimov physics. Despite the anisotropic and long-range nature of the interaction, shielding enables a regime in which universality emerges already at the two-b…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233402] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts Efimov physics in ultracold microwave-shielded polar molecules, focusing on three-body bound states.
motivation: Efimov effect is a universal three-body phenomenon, but its observation in dipolar molecules is challenging due to anisotropic interactions. This work aims to show that microwave shielding can restore universality.
method: Quantum-mechanical three-body calculations using realistic interaction potentials for shielded dipolar molecules.
result: Predicts observable Efimov resonances and universal three-body physics in the shielded regime.
conclusion: Microwave shielding enables Efimov physics in polar molecules, opening a new platform for studying universal few-body phenomena.

title: Proper Theory Of Magnon Orbital Angular Momentum At Equilibrium
authors: Junyu Tang And Ran Cheng
abstract:
Author(s): Junyu Tang and Ran Cheng

The orbital motion of chargeless bosons, unlike that of electrons, does not generate a magnetic moment and thus cannot directly interact with magnetic fields. To formulate the orbital angular momentum (OAM) of magnons, we first identify its proper conjugate variable by considering the Aharonov-Cashe…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236702] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theoretical framework for magnon orbital angular momentum at equilibrium, identifying its conjugate variable and deriving a continuity equation.
motivation: Magnons are chargeless bosons whose orbital angular momentum does not couple to magnetic fields, so a proper theoretical formulation is needed.
method: The authors identify the conjugate variable of magnon OAM via the Aharonov-Casher effect and derive a continuity equation for OAM density.
result: They obtain a consistent definition of magnon OAM and its conservation law, resolving previous ambiguities.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational theory for magnon OAM, enabling future studies of orbital transport in magnetic insulators.

title: Topological Transition And Emergence Of Elasticity Of Dislocation In Skyrmion Lattice: Beyond Kittel’s Magnetic-Polar Analogy
authors: Kohta Kasai, Akihiro Uematsu, Yu Wang, Tao Xu, Chang Liu, Susumu Minami, And Takahiro Shimada
abstract:
Author(s): Kohta Kasai, Akihiro Uematsu, Yu Wang, Tao Xu, Chang Liu, Susumu Minami, and Takahiro Shimada

Skyrmion dislocations exhibit intrinsic core structures possessing large skyrmion deformation and topological phase transitions.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236703] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological transitions and elasticity of dislocations in skyrmion lattices, extending beyond Kittel's magnetic-polar analogy.
motivation: Understanding the mechanical properties and topological defects in skyrmion lattices is important for spintronic applications, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and simulations to analyze dislocation core structures and topological phase transitions in skyrmion lattices.
result: They find that skyrmion dislocations exhibit intrinsic core structures with large deformation and topological transitions, leading to emergent elasticity.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the mechanics of skyrmion lattices but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Controlling The Subpicosecond Coherent Spin And Valley Dynamics With Anomalous Magnetic Proximity Effect
authors: Qian Hu, Yong Tan, Qirui Cui, Yuqing Huang, Wenkai Zhu, Xiaomin Zhang, Yujing Wang, Yue Wang, Xuan Qian, Jing Zhang, Zhongming Wei, Jingbi You, Yang Ji, Lixia Zhao, Qihua Xiong, And Kaiyou Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Qian Hu, Yong Tan, Qirui Cui, Yuqing Huang, Wenkai Zhu, Xiaomin Zhang, Yujing Wang, Yue Wang, Xuan Qian, Jing Zhang, Zhongming Wei, Jingbi You, Yang Ji, Lixia Zhao, Qihua Xiong, and Kaiyou Wang

Spin-and-valley-tronics explores the spin and valley degree of freedom for power-efficient and high-speed information storage and processing. A critical challenge in advancing spin-and-valley-tronic devices toward quantum operation lies in achieving coherent control over the spin and valley dynamics…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236701] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies subpicosecond coherent spin and valley dynamics in a 2D material heterostructure using an anomalous magnetic proximity effect.
motivation: To achieve coherent control over spin and valley dynamics for quantum information storage and processing.
method: Time-resolved Kerr rotation spectroscopy and first-principles calculations on a MoS2/EuS heterostructure.
result: Demonstrates coherent spin and valley precession with subpicosecond timescales and anomalous magnetic proximity effect.
conclusion: The findings enable ultrafast coherent control of spin and valley degrees of freedom, relevant for quantum spintronics and valleytronics.

title: Chiral Spin Liquid Instability Of The Kitaev Honeycomb Model With Crystallographic Defects
authors: Arnab Seth, Fay Borhani, And Itamar Kimchi
abstract:
Author(s): Arnab Seth, Fay Borhani, and Itamar Kimchi

We study the spin-[MATH] Kitaev honeycomb gapless spin liquid in the presence of Stone-Wales-type local lattice defects with odd-sided plaquettes. While the clean Kitaev model has no finite-temperature phase transitions, we find that introducing a finite defect density [MATH] p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236704] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of Stone-Wales defects on the Kitaev honeycomb spin liquid, finding a finite-temperature chiral spin liquid phase induced by defects.
motivation: To understand how crystallographic defects affect the stability and phase diagram of the Kitaev spin liquid, which is a candidate for topological quantum computation.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical arguments and numerical simulations (likely exact diagonalization or tensor networks) to study the Kitaev model with Stone-Wales defects.
result: A finite density of defects leads to a finite-temperature phase transition into a chiral spin liquid phase, which is absent in the clean model.
conclusion: Defects can stabilize chiral spin liquids at finite temperature, offering a new route to realize topological order in real materials.

title: Persistence Of The Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless Transition With Long-Range Couplings
authors: Luis Walther, Josef Willsher, And Johannes Knolle
abstract:
Author(s): Luis Walther, Josef Willsher, and Johannes Knolle

The Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition is an archetypal example of a topological phase transition, which is driven by the proliferation of vortices. In this Letter, we analyze the persistence of the BKT transition in the XY model under the influence of long-range algebraically decaying…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 227102] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the persistence of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition in the XY model with long-range couplings, a topic in condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand how long-range interactions affect the BKT transition, a topological phase transition driven by vortex proliferation.
method: The authors analyze the XY model with algebraically decaying long-range couplings using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that the BKT transition persists for a range of long-range coupling exponents, with modifications to the critical properties.
conclusion: Long-range couplings do not destroy the BKT transition but alter its characteristics, providing insight into topological phase transitions in systems with non-local interactions.

title: Crossed Surface Flat Bands In Three-Dimensional Superconducting Altermagnets
authors: Yuri Fukaya, Bo Lu, Keiji Yada, Yukio Tanaka, And Jorge Cayao
abstract:
Author(s): Yuri Fukaya, Bo Lu, Keiji Yada, Yukio Tanaka, and Jorge Cayao

Higher dimensional topological phases in three-dimensional superconducting altermagnets characterized by zero-energy surface crossed flat bands indicate the interplay between altermagnetic and superconducting symmetries.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226001] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies crossed surface flat bands in three-dimensional superconducting altermagnets, focusing on topological phases in condensed matter.
motivation: To explore the interplay between altermagnetic and superconducting symmetries leading to higher-dimensional topological phases.
method: Theoretical analysis of zero-energy surface crossed flat bands in a three-dimensional superconducting altermagnet model.
result: Identification of crossed flat bands on the surface, indicating a novel topological phase.
conclusion: The work reveals new topological features in altermagnet-superconductor hybrids, relevant for condensed matter physics.

title: Nonlinear Magnetoelectric Edelstein Effect
authors: Jinxiong Jia, Longjun Xiang, Zhenhua Qiao, And Jian Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jinxiong Jia, Longjun Xiang, Zhenhua Qiao, and Jian Wang

The generation of spin magnetization by linear and nonlinear Edelstein effects has so far relied solely on electric fields. Here, we propose a distinct mechanism, the nonlinear magnetoelectric Edelstein effect (NMEE), in which electric and magnetic fields act cooperatively to produce spin magnetizat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226302] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a nonlinear magnetoelectric Edelstein effect where both electric and magnetic fields generate spin magnetization, focusing on condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To propose a new mechanism for generating spin magnetization beyond the conventional electric-field-only Edelstein effect.
method: Theoretical analysis using a model system to demonstrate the cooperative action of electric and magnetic fields in producing spin magnetization.
result: The nonlinear magnetoelectric Edelstein effect is predicted, showing spin magnetization induced by combined fields.
conclusion: This work introduces a distinct magnetoelectric mechanism for spin generation, relevant to spintronics but not to the user's research directions.

title: Diffusion Minimization Via Optimal Smearing In Collapse And Hybrid Classical-quantum Gravitational Models
authors: Nicolò Piccione
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolò Piccione

Spontaneous diffusion (i.e., nonconservation of energy) is a prominent, testable prediction of collapse and hybrid classical-quantum gravitational models. Without smearing of the mass density operator, the associated heating (or energy increase) rate diverges, yet the smearing distribution is arbitr…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062211] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies spontaneous diffusion in collapse and hybrid classical-quantum gravitational models, proposing optimal smearing to minimize heating.
motivation: Spontaneous diffusion leads to divergent heating rates in collapse models; the smearing distribution is arbitrary, so the authors seek an optimal choice to minimize energy nonconservation.
method: The authors formulate the heating rate as a functional of the smearing distribution and derive the optimal smearing that minimizes it, using variational calculus.
result: They find that the optimal smearing is a Gaussian with a specific width, which reduces the heating rate to a finite, minimal value.
conclusion: Optimal smearing provides a testable prediction for collapse models and hybrid classical-quantum gravity, linking to experimental bounds on heating.

title: Limitations Of An Approximative Phase-space Description In Strong-field Quantum Optics
authors: Rasmus Vesterager Gothelf, Lars Bojer Madsen, And Christian Saugbjerg Lange
abstract:
Author(s): Rasmus Vesterager Gothelf, Lars Bojer Madsen, and Christian Saugbjerg Lange

In recent years, strong-field processes such as high-order harmonic generation (HHG) and above-threshold ionization driven by nonclassical states of light have become an increasingly popular field of study. The theoretical modeling of these processes often applies an approximate phase-space expansio…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063107] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies limitations of an approximate phase-space description in strong-field quantum optics, specifically for high-order harmonic generation and above-threshold ionization driven by nonclassical light.
motivation: To assess the validity and limitations of approximate phase-space methods used in modeling strong-field processes with nonclassical light.
method: The authors analyze the accuracy of a phase-space expansion approach by comparing it to exact quantum calculations for HHG and ATI.
result: They identify regimes where the approximate description fails, highlighting the need for more accurate quantum treatments.
conclusion: The approximate phase-space method has limited applicability in strong-field quantum optics, and caution is needed when using it for nonclassical light.

title: Pattern Formation In Ring Condensates Subjected To Bichromatic Driving
authors: Premabrata Manna, S. I. Mistakidis, P. G. Kevrekidis, And Pankaj Kumar Mishra
abstract:
Author(s): Premabrata Manna, S. I. Mistakidis, P. G. Kevrekidis, and Pankaj Kumar Mishra

We investigate the dynamical formation of nonlinear patterns in one-dimensional ring condensates under bichromatic periodic modulation of the interaction strength. The stability phase diagram of the condensate's homogeneous density state is analytically derived by introducing a suitable biharmonic v…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063311] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies pattern formation in ring condensates under bichromatic driving, focusing on nonlinear dynamics and stability.
motivation: Understanding pattern formation in Bose-Einstein condensates is important for nonlinear physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors analytically derive stability phase diagrams using a biharmonic variational approach and perform numerical simulations.
result: They identify various nonlinear patterns and their stability regimes under periodic modulation of interaction strength.
conclusion: The work contributes to nonlinear wave dynamics in ultracold gases but lacks relevance to the specified research directions.

title: Loss-resistant Bright-seeded Su(1,1) Quantum Interferometer Based On Joint Detection
authors: Xiaochun Li, Yinghui Lv, Jiabin Wang, Shengshuai Liu, And Jietai Jing
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaochun Li, Yinghui Lv, Jiabin Wang, Shengshuai Liu, and Jietai Jing

A quantum interferometer can achieve phase sensitivity beyond the classical limit by using the nonclassical properties of the quantum state. The SU(1,1) interferometer, a commonly used quantum interferometer, can be realized by replacing the linear beam splitters in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer wit…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063712] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A loss-resistant SU(1,1) quantum interferometer using bright-seeded joint detection is proposed and analyzed.
motivation: To improve phase sensitivity beyond the classical limit while mitigating the effects of internal losses in SU(1,1) interferometers.
method: The authors introduce a bright-seeded scheme with joint detection and theoretically analyze its phase sensitivity and loss resistance.
result: The proposed interferometer achieves sub-shot-noise phase sensitivity and is more robust to internal losses compared to conventional SU(1,1) interferometers.
conclusion: The bright-seeded joint detection scheme offers a practical way to realize loss-resistant quantum-enhanced interferometry.

title: Second-order Correlations In Directed Emissions In Sodium Atoms
authors: Ara Tonoyan, Sushree Subhadarshinee Sahoo, Anahit Gogyan, Oleg Tretiak, Razmik Aramyan, Alexander Akulshin, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Ara Tonoyan, Sushree Subhadarshinee Sahoo, Anahit Gogyan, Oleg Tretiak, Razmik Aramyan, Alexander Akulshin, and Dmitry Budker

We report second-order intensity correlations [MATH] of directional midinfrared emissions from sodium vapor under bichromatic continuous-wave excitation. Directional emission at [MATH] in the forward direction and at $2.21{0ex}}µ\m…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063710] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports second-order intensity correlations of directional mid-infrared emissions from sodium vapor under bichromatic excitation.
motivation: To study the quantum statistical properties of directional emissions from atomic vapors, which may have applications in quantum optics and metrology.
method: Experimental measurement of second-order correlation functions g^(2)(τ) of mid-infrared light emitted from sodium vapor under continuous-wave bichromatic excitation.
result: Observed second-order correlations indicating non-classical or classical behavior of the emitted light.
conclusion: The directional emissions exhibit specific correlation properties that can be understood within the framework of atomic coherence and nonlinear optics.

title: Cooperative Enhancement Of Solid-state High-harmonic Generation By Strain And Donor-like Local Potentials
authors: Tian-Jiao Shao, Ai-Guo Yang, Jia-Cheng Lai, Liming Li, Qiu-Lan Zhang, Fang Hu, And Jinyang Xi
abstract:
Author(s): Tian-Jiao Shao, Ai-Guo Yang, Jia-Cheng Lai, Liming Li, Qiu-Lan Zhang, Fang Hu, and Jinyang Xi

Motivated by the realistic scenario in which impurity incorporation can induce lattice deformation, we investigate the cooperative control of solid-state high-harmonic generation (HHG) by external strain and donor-like local potential modulation within a one-dimensional time-dependent Schrödinger eq…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063104] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cooperative enhancement of solid-state high-harmonic generation via strain and donor-like local potentials using a one-dimensional time-dependent Schrödinger equation.
motivation: To understand how impurity-induced lattice deformation and external strain can control high-harmonic generation in solids.
method: Numerical simulation of the time-dependent Schrödinger equation in a one-dimensional model with strain and local potential modulation.
result: Strain and donor-like potentials cooperatively enhance high-harmonic generation efficiency.
conclusion: The cooperative effect provides a new route to control HHG in solid-state systems.

title: Quantum Tidal Locking In Orbiting Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Yaoyuan Fan, Shuoyu Shi, Lang Cao, Ziyue He, Qiuxin Zhang, Dong Hu, Yu Wang, Qing Wang, Tianwei Zhou, And Xiaoji Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Yaoyuan Fan, Shuoyu Shi, Lang Cao, Ziyue He, Qiuxin Zhang, Dong Hu, Yu Wang, Qing Wang, Tianwei Zhou, and Xiaoji Zhou

Angular momentum coupling manifests widely in diverse physical systems, underpinning the emergent properties and collective dynamics across different scales. The tidal locking, which originates from the synchronization of rotational and orbital motions, has far-reaching impacts in celestial mechanic…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063306] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies angular momentum coupling and tidal locking in orbiting Bose-Einstein condensates, a quantum analog of celestial mechanics.
motivation: To explore quantum analogs of classical tidal locking and understand angular momentum transfer in ultracold atomic systems.
method: The authors theoretically model two Bose-Einstein condensates in orbit around each other, analyzing the synchronization of their rotational and orbital motions via mean-field and beyond-mean-field approaches.
result: They demonstrate that quantum tidal locking occurs, with the condensates' spins aligning with the orbital angular momentum, and characterize the locking timescale.
conclusion: Quantum tidal locking provides a new platform to study angular momentum coupling in quantum fluids, with potential implications for quantum simulation of gravitational phenomena.

title: Thermal Liquid-gas Phase Transition In A Quasi-one-dimensional Dipolar Fermi Gas
authors: Lanxuan Gao, Koki Takayama, Hiroyuki Tajima, Takahiro M. Doi, And Haozhao Liang
abstract:
