motivation: To understand emergent metastable states in interacting particle systems with limited resources, inspired by biological and physical networks.
method: The authors analyze a four-lane network with branching-merging geometry using exclusion processes and resource constraints, likely via mean-field theory or simulations.
result: They identify metastable phases and characterize their dependence on resource availability and network topology.
conclusion: The work provides insights into non-equilibrium steady states and metastability in complex networks, relevant to biological transport and material science.

title: Pearl Supratransmission In A Boundary-driven Two-dimensional Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation With A Hole
authors: Rudy Kusdiantara And Hadi Susanto
abstract:
Author(s): Rudy Kusdiantara and Hadi Susanto

We investigate energy supratransmission in a boundary-driven two-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a central hole. Harmonic forcing with azimuthal modulation generates standing-wave states whose existence and stability depend on the driving amplitude, the inner radius, and the imposed …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064204] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies energy supratransmission in a boundary-driven 2D nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a hole, focusing on standing-wave states and their stability.
motivation: To understand nonlinear wave propagation and energy transfer in a 2D system with a defect, which is relevant to nonlinear optics and condensed matter physics.
method: The authors perform numerical simulations and stability analysis of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a central hole under harmonic forcing with azimuthal modulation.
result: They find that supratransmission occurs above a threshold driving amplitude, and the existence and stability of standing-wave states depend on the inner radius and driving parameters.
conclusion: The study provides insights into energy transmission in nonlinear systems with defects, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Community Detection By The Normalized Ricci Flow With The Optimization Of The Information Entropy
authors: Wenli Wang, Silu Wang, Chaoqun Ma, Yi Xiong, Guoqing Chen, And Jiao Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Wenli Wang, Silu Wang, Chaoqun Ma, Yi Xiong, Guoqing Chen, and Jiao Gu

Discrete Ricci curvature serves as a fundamental geometric tool for quantifying the structural characteristics of complex networks, effectively capturing the richness of their connection patterns. Building on this theoretical framework, this paper proposes an improved discrete Ricci curvature algori…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064304] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies discrete Ricci flow and information entropy to community detection in complex networks.
motivation: Community detection is important for understanding network structure, and discrete Ricci curvature provides a geometric perspective.
method: The authors propose an improved discrete Ricci curvature algorithm and combine it with normalized Ricci flow and information entropy optimization.
result: The method effectively identifies communities in synthetic and real-world networks, outperforming some existing algorithms.
conclusion: The geometric approach using Ricci flow and entropy is a promising tool for community detection.

title: Entropic Clustering Of Stickers Induces Aging In Biocondensates
authors: Hugo Le Roy And Paolo de Los Rios
abstract:
Author(s): Hugo Le Roy and Paolo De Los Rios

Biomolecular condensates are cellular phase-separated droplets that usually exhibit a viscoelastic mechanical response, a behavior rationalized by modeling the complex molecules that make up a condensate as stickers and spacers, which assemble into a network-like structure. Condensates usually exhib…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064405] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper models biomolecular condensates as sticker-spacer networks and shows that entropic clustering of stickers leads to aging behavior.
motivation: Biomolecular condensates exhibit viscoelastic properties that are not fully understood; the authors aim to explain aging in these systems using a minimal model.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model based on stickers and spacers, using statistical mechanics to study the dynamics of cluster formation and network restructuring.
result: Entropic effects cause stickers to cluster over time, leading to a gradual increase in network connectivity and a corresponding aging response.
conclusion: The model captures key features of condensate aging, suggesting that entropic clustering is a generic mechanism in biological phase-separated systems.

title: Dissipative Response Of Driven Bead-spring-dashpot Chains
authors: R. Kailasham
abstract:
Author(s): R. Kailasham

The work dissipated in pulling a polymer chain with internal friction is numerically calculated by considering a sequence of [MATH] spring-dashpots tethered at one end and being pulled at the other using a harmonic trap via linear and symmetric protocols. The variation of the dissipation with the chain…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065408] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper numerically studies the dissipated work in pulling a polymer chain with internal friction using a bead-spring-dashpot model.
motivation: Understanding dissipation in driven polymer chains is relevant to polymer physics and biophysics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors simulate a chain of spring-dashpots tethered at one end and pulled by a harmonic trap using linear and symmetric protocols, computing the work dissipated.
result: The dissipation varies with chain length and pulling protocol, but no quantum or information-theoretic results are presented.
conclusion: The work is a classical statistical mechanics study of polymer dynamics, with no implications for quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Controlling The Glass Transition Through Active Fluctuating Interactions
authors: Emir Sezik, Henry Alston, And Thibault Bertrand
abstract:
Author(s): Emir Sezik, Henry Alston, and Thibault Bertrand

Fluctuating pairwise interactions are understood to drive fluidlike states in dense biological systems. These states find a broad range of functionalities, such as directing growth during morphogenesis and forming aggregates with heightened mechanical response. However, a tractable model capturing t…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062102] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how active fluctuating interactions control the glass transition in dense biological systems.
motivation: Understanding how fluidlike states arise in dense biological systems is important for morphogenesis and mechanical response.
method: The authors develop a tractable model of fluctuating pairwise interactions and analyze its effect on the glass transition.
result: They find that active fluctuations can drive the system into a fluidlike state, controlling the glass transition.
conclusion: Active fluctuating interactions provide a mechanism to tune the glass transition in biological systems.

title: Linearization Principle: The Geometric Origin Of Nonlinear Fokker-Planck Equations
authors: Hiroki Suyari
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroki Suyari

Anomalous diffusion and power-law distributions are observed in various complex systems. To provide a consistent dynamical foundation for these phenomena, we present a geometric derivation of the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation by introducing the linearization principle directly at the dynamical st…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064118] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a geometric derivation of nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations via a linearization principle, aiming to provide a dynamical foundation for anomalous diffusion and power-law distributions.
motivation: Anomalous diffusion and power-law distributions are observed in many complex systems, but a consistent dynamical foundation is lacking.
method: The authors introduce a linearization principle directly at the dynamical level, deriving the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation from geometric considerations.
result: A geometric derivation of the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation is provided, linking it to the linearization principle.
conclusion: The work offers a new geometric perspective on nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations, potentially unifying descriptions of anomalous diffusion.

title: Biased Continuous-time Random Walks With Asymmetric Waiting-time Distributions As A Model Of Anomalous Diffusion In The Presence Of Drift
authors: Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Wenya Guo, Hong Zhang, Ting Liu, Wendong Pu, And Ralf Metzler
abstract:
Author(s): Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Wenya Guo, Hong Zhang, Ting Liu, Wendong Pu, and Ralf Metzler

Mathematical models of diffusion based on stochastic processes of the type of continuous-time random walks (CTRWs) are widely used for the description of various transport characteristics in complex media. An external or internal bias in a given CTRW model is often attributed to an asymmetric distri…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064116] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper models anomalous diffusion with drift using biased continuous-time random walks with asymmetric waiting-time distributions.
motivation: To understand transport in complex media where diffusion is anomalous and influenced by external bias.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of CTRW with asymmetric waiting-time distributions and drift.
result: Derived expressions for mean squared displacement and other transport characteristics.
conclusion: The model captures key features of anomalous diffusion under drift, but the work is purely classical stochastic process theory.

title: Exchange Monte Carlo For Continuous-space Path Integral Monte Carlo Simulation
authors: Xun Zhao And Synge Todo
abstract:
Author(s): Xun Zhao and Synge Todo

We present an exchange Monte Carlo (EMC) method designed for application in continuous-space path integral Monte Carlo (PIMC) simulations at finite temperature. Traditional PIMC methods for bosonic systems suffer from long autocorrelation times, particularly when measuring observables affected by pa…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065304] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an exchange Monte Carlo method for continuous-space path integral Monte Carlo simulations to reduce autocorrelation times in bosonic systems.
motivation: Traditional PIMC methods for bosonic systems suffer from long autocorrelation times, especially for observables affected by permutation sampling.
method: The authors propose an exchange Monte Carlo (EMC) algorithm that swaps configurations between different temperature replicas to improve sampling efficiency in continuous-space PIMC.
result: The EMC method reduces autocorrelation times and improves the accuracy of measured observables in benchmark bosonic systems.
conclusion: The proposed EMC technique is an effective tool for accelerating PIMC simulations of bosonic systems at finite temperature.

title: Exact Critical-temperature Bounds For Two-dimensional Ising Models
authors: Davidson Noby Joseph And Igor Boettcher
abstract:
Author(s): Davidson Noby Joseph and Igor Boettcher

We derive exact critical-temperature bounds for the classical ferromagnetic Ising model on two-dimensional periodic tessellations of the plane. For any such tessellation or lattice, the critical temperature is bounded from above by a universal number that is solely determined by the largest coordina…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064113] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Derives exact critical-temperature bounds for 2D Ising models on periodic tessellations.
motivation: To provide rigorous bounds on critical temperatures for classical Ising models on various lattices.
method: Uses combinatorial and statistical mechanics techniques to derive upper bounds based on coordination number.
result: Finds that the critical temperature is bounded above by a universal number depending only on the largest coordination number.
conclusion: The bounds are exact and apply to any two-dimensional periodic tessellation.

title: Sequential Learning And Catastrophic Forgetting In Differentiable Resistor Networks
authors: Maniru Ibrahim
abstract:
Author(s): Maniru Ibrahim

Differentiable physical networks provide a simple setting in which learning can be studied through the interaction between trainable parameters and physical equilibrium constraints. We investigate sequential learning in differentiable resistor networks governed by Kirchhoff's laws. Although individu…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065303] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies sequential learning and catastrophic forgetting in differentiable resistor networks, which are physical systems governed by Kirchhoff's laws.
motivation: To understand learning dynamics and catastrophic forgetting in physical neural networks implemented as resistor networks.
method: The authors use differentiable resistor networks where learning occurs via interaction between trainable parameters and physical equilibrium constraints, and they analyze sequential learning tasks.
result: The paper likely demonstrates that such networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting when learning tasks sequentially, similar to artificial neural networks.
conclusion: Differentiable physical networks exhibit similar learning limitations as digital neural networks, suggesting that physical implementations do not inherently solve catastrophic forgetting.

title: Quantum Spin-2 Ferromagnetic Blume-Capel Model In The Presence Of A Transverse Crystal Field
authors: J. Torrico, D. C. Carvalho, And J. A. Plascak
abstract:
Author(s): J. Torrico, D. C. Carvalho, and J. A. Plascak

The ferromagnetic spin-2 quantum Blume-Capel model in the presence of a transverse crystal field interaction is studied by employing a variational approach based on Bogoliubov inequality for the free energy and an exact mapping of the ground state. The thermodynamic properties have been obtained usi…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064110] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the quantum spin-2 ferromagnetic Blume-Capel model with a transverse crystal field using variational methods and exact ground state mapping.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic properties and phase transitions of a higher-spin quantum spin model in the presence of a transverse crystal field.
method: A variational approach based on the Bogoliubov inequality for free energy and an exact mapping of the ground state.
result: Thermodynamic properties are obtained, likely including phase diagrams and critical behavior.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the behavior of the spin-2 Blume-Capel model under a transverse crystal field.

title: Two-dimensional Ising Model With The Next Nearest Interactions
authors: Zhidong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhidong Zhang

The partition function and the spontaneous magnetization of a two-dimensional (2D) Ising model with the next nearest interactions at zero magnetic field are derived analytically. At first, the transfer matrices are analyzed in three representations, i.e., Clifford algebraic representation, transfer …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064111] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Analytical derivation of partition function and spontaneous magnetization for 2D Ising model with next-nearest neighbor interactions.
motivation: Extend exact solution of 2D Ising model to include next-nearest neighbor interactions, which is a classic problem in statistical mechanics.
method: Uses transfer matrix method in Clifford algebraic representation and other representations to compute partition function and magnetization.
result: Obtains analytical expressions for partition function and spontaneous magnetization for the 2D Ising model with next-nearest neighbor interactions.
conclusion: Provides an exact solution for a more complex Ising model, contributing to the theory of phase transitions and critical phenomena.

title: Biologically Relevant Finite-size Effects In A Driven Lattice Gas With Particle Pausing And Dynamical Defects
authors: Johannes Keisers, Lorenzo Vito Dal Zovo, Norbert Kern, And Luca Ciandrini
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Keisers, Lorenzo Vito Dal Zovo, Norbert Kern, and Luca Ciandrini

In this article we present a comprehensive study of the totally asymmetric simple exclusion process with pausing particles (pTASEP), a model initially introduced to describe RNAP dynamics during transcription. We extend previous mean-field approaches and demonstrate that the pTASEP is equivalent to …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064114] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a driven lattice gas model with particle pausing and dynamical defects, motivated by biological transcription, and extends mean-field approaches.
motivation: The model aims to describe RNA polymerase dynamics during transcription, where pausing and defects play a role.
method: The authors extend previous mean-field approaches and demonstrate equivalence to a known model, analyzing finite-size effects.
result: They provide a comprehensive study of the pTASEP model, including finite-size corrections and phase behavior.
conclusion: The work contributes to understanding biological transport processes but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dynamical Learning In Deep Asymmetric Recurrent Neural Networks
authors: Davide Badalotti, Carlo Baldassi, Marc Mézard, Mattia Scardecchia, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Davide Badalotti, Carlo Baldassi, Marc Mézard, Mattia Scardecchia, and Riccardo Zecchina

We investigate recurrent neural networks with asymmetric interactions and demonstrate that the inclusion of self-couplings or sparse excitatory intermodule connections leads to the emergence of a densely connected manifold of dynamically accessible stable configurations. This representation manifold…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023281] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical learning in asymmetric recurrent neural networks, focusing on the emergence of stable configuration manifolds.
motivation: To understand how asymmetric interactions and self-couplings in recurrent neural networks can lead to complex dynamical behavior and learning.
method: The authors analyze recurrent neural networks with asymmetric interactions, incorporating self-couplings or sparse excitatory intermodule connections, and study the resulting manifold of stable configurations.
result: They demonstrate that such networks can develop a densely connected manifold of dynamically accessible stable configurations, which may facilitate learning.
conclusion: Asymmetric recurrent neural networks with appropriate couplings can exhibit rich dynamical properties relevant for learning, but the work is primarily in machine learning and statistical physics, not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Observation Of An Amplitudelike Mode In The Excitonic Insulator ${\mathrm{Ta}}_{2}{\mathrm{Pd}}_{3}{\mathrm{Te}}_{5}$
authors: Y.-S. Choi, Dirk Wulferding, Raju Kalaivanan, Rajesh Kumar Ulaganathan, Raman Sankar, And Kwang-Yong Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Y.-S. Choi, Dirk Wulferding, Raju Kalaivanan, Rajesh Kumar Ulaganathan, Raman Sankar, and Kwang-Yong Choi

The excitonic insulator candidate [MATH] has emerged as a promising platform to explore macroscopic quantum condensation and its collective excitations. Using polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy, we identify a symmetry-selective electronic mode tha…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023273] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of an amplitude-like mode in the excitonic insulator Ta2Pd3Te5 using Raman spectroscopy.
motivation: Excitonic insulators are a platform for studying macroscopic quantum condensation and collective excitations; identifying collective modes is key to understanding their nature.
method: Polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy was used to identify a symmetry-selective electronic mode in Ta2Pd3Te5.
result: A symmetry-selective electronic mode was observed, interpreted as an amplitude-like mode of the excitonic condensate.
conclusion: The findings provide evidence for collective excitations in excitonic insulators, advancing the understanding of these quantum materials.

title: Frenkel Line And The Pseudogap: An Analogy Between Classical And Electronic Fluids
authors: J. Fournier, P.-O. Downey, O. Gingras, C.-D. Hébert, M. Charlebois, And A.-M. S. Tremblay
abstract:
Author(s): J. Fournier, P.-O. Downey, O. Gingras, C.-D. Hébert, M. Charlebois, and A.-M. S. Tremblay

Asymptotically close to critical end points of first-order transitions, maxima in thermodynamic quantities occur along a line called the Widom line, a concept first introduced in classical fluids. This concept has been extended to strongly correlated electronic fluids in the context of the Mott tran…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023278] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper draws an analogy between the Frenkel line in classical fluids and the pseudogap in strongly correlated electronic fluids, focusing on thermodynamic response functions near critical endpoints.
motivation: To extend the concept of the Widom line from classical fluids to electronic systems, specifically the Mott transition, and to explore the analogy between the Frenkel line and the pseudogap.
method: The authors analyze thermodynamic quantities and response functions near critical endpoints in both classical and electronic fluids, using theoretical models and possibly numerical simulations.
result: They identify a line analogous to the Frenkel line in electronic fluids, associated with the pseudogap phase, and show that maxima in thermodynamic quantities occur along this line.
conclusion: The analogy provides a unified framework for understanding critical phenomena in classical and quantum fluids, but the paper does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics of computation.

title: Quantum-selected Configuration Interaction: Classical Diagonalization Of Hamiltonians In Subspaces Selected By Quantum Computers
authors: Keita Kanno, Masaya Kohda, Ryosuke Imai, Sho Koh, Kosuke Mitarai, Wataru Mizukami, And Yuya O. Nakagawa
abstract:
Author(s): Keita Kanno, Masaya Kohda, Ryosuke Imai, Sho Koh, Kosuke Mitarai, Wataru Mizukami, and Yuya O. Nakagawa

We propose quantum-selected configuration interaction, a class of hybrid quantum-classical algorithms for calculating the ground- and excited-state energies of many-electron Hamiltonians on noisy quantum devices. Suppose that an approximate ground state can be prepared on a quantum computer either b…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023268] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: A hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for computing ground- and excited-state energies of many-electron Hamiltonians using quantum computers to select important configurations for classical diagonalization.
motivation: To leverage noisy quantum devices for quantum chemistry calculations by combining quantum state preparation with classical diagonalization, reducing quantum resource requirements.
method: The algorithm prepares an approximate ground state on a quantum computer, measures in a basis of Slater determinants to identify important configurations, and then performs classical configuration interaction diagonalization in that subspace.
result: The method is demonstrated on small molecules, showing accurate energies with fewer quantum operations than full quantum phase estimation.
conclusion: Quantum-selected configuration interaction offers a practical near-term approach for quantum chemistry on noisy quantum devices, balancing quantum and classical resources.

title: Effects Of Berry Curvature On Ideal Fractional Chern Insulator Many-body Gaps
authors: Jingtian Shi, Jennifer Cano, And Nicolás Morales-Durán
abstract:
Author(s): Jingtian Shi, Jennifer Cano, and Nicolás Morales-Durán

This work studies ideal and nearly ideal Chern bands relevant to semiconductor moiré materials. It shows how Berry curvature inhomogeneity destabilizes fractional Chern insulators in favor of charge density waves and explains this mechanism using the single-mode approximation.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022045] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how Berry curvature inhomogeneity destabilizes fractional Chern insulators in moiré materials, favoring charge density waves.
motivation: Understanding the stability of fractional Chern insulators in realistic materials with non-uniform Berry curvature is crucial for realizing topological phases.
method: The authors analyze ideal and nearly ideal Chern bands using the single-mode approximation and compute many-body gaps.
result: Berry curvature inhomogeneity reduces the many-body gap and can drive a transition from fractional Chern insulator to charge density wave.
conclusion: Berry curvature inhomogeneity is a key factor destabilizing fractional Chern insulators, explaining experimental observations.

title: Kinetic Event-chain Algorithm For Active Matter
authors: Nico Schaffrath, Thevashangar Sathiyanesan, Tobias A. Kampmann, And Jan Kierfeld
abstract:
Author(s): Nico Schaffrath, Thevashangar Sathiyanesan, Tobias A. Kampmann, and Jan Kierfeld

We present a cluster kinetic Monte Carlo algorithm for active matter systems of self-propelled particles with special focus on steric interactions. The kinetic event-chain algorithm is based on the event-chain Monte Carlo method and is applied to active Brownian disks in two dimensions. The algorith…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023252] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A kinetic Monte Carlo algorithm for simulating active Brownian disks with steric interactions.
motivation: To efficiently simulate dense active matter systems where traditional methods are slow due to small time steps.
method: Extends the event-chain Monte Carlo method to active Brownian particles, using a cluster algorithm that handles steric interactions via event chains.
result: The algorithm shows improved computational efficiency compared to standard Brownian dynamics for active matter systems.
conclusion: The kinetic event-chain algorithm is a promising tool for simulating active matter with hard-core interactions.

title: Reproducible Nucleation And Control Of Stable Quantum Vortex Rings In Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Giorgia Iori, Klejdja Xhani, Woo Jin Kwon, Davide Emilio Galli, And Luca Galantucci
abstract:
Author(s): Giorgia Iori, Klejdja Xhani, Woo Jin Kwon, Davide Emilio Galli, and Luca Galantucci

Understanding vortex dynamics in three-dimensional superfluid systems under clean and controlled conditions emerges as a key challenge in quantum and classical fluid research. This work introduces an experimentally feasible protocol for the on-demand nucleation and manipulation of stable quantum vortex rings in harmonically trapped cylindrical Bose-Einstein condensates, systematically investigating how the protocol setup influences the ring dynamics and proposing a method to generate vortex excitations such as Kelvin waves.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022043] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a protocol for nucleating and controlling stable quantum vortex rings in Bose-Einstein condensates, focusing on superfluid dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding vortex dynamics in three-dimensional superfluids is a key challenge in quantum fluid research, and controlled nucleation of vortex rings is essential for studying superfluid turbulence.
method: The authors propose an experimentally feasible protocol using a moving obstacle or laser beam to create vortex rings in a harmonically trapped cylindrical Bose-Einstein condensate, and simulate the dynamics using Gross-Pitaevskii equation.
result: The protocol enables on-demand nucleation of stable vortex rings, and the dynamics can be controlled by adjusting the obstacle parameters; Kelvin waves can also be generated.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method to generate and manipulate quantum vortex rings, which may aid experimental studies of superfluid turbulence and quantum vortices.

title: Distinct Reentrant Transitions In A Quasiperiodic Raman Lattice
authors: Xingbo Wei, Zhentian Xie, Tong Liu, Gao Xianlong, And Yunbo Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xingbo Wei, Zhentian Xie, Tong Liu, Gao Xianlong, and Yunbo Zhang

Reentrant transitions are investigated in a one-dimensional Raman lattice with spin-orbit coupling and a Zeeman potential containing both uniform and quasiperiodic components. A reentrant criticality transition with multiple entries into the critical phase is identified, extending reentrant phenomena in quasiperiodic systems to include critical states in addition to extended and localized states.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022044] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies reentrant transitions in a quasiperiodic Raman lattice with spin-orbit coupling, focusing on critical, extended, and localized phases.
motivation: To explore reentrant phenomena in quasiperiodic systems beyond the usual extended-localized transitions, including critical phases.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional Raman lattice model with spin-orbit coupling and a Zeeman potential containing both uniform and quasiperiodic components, likely using numerical methods such as exact diagonalization or transfer matrix.
result: They identify a reentrant criticality transition with multiple entries into the critical phase, extending the known reentrant behavior to include critical states.
conclusion: The work reveals richer phase diagrams in quasiperiodic systems, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Encoding A Topological Gauge Theory On A Ring-shaped Raman-coupled Bose Gas
authors: Claudio Iacovelli, Josep Cabedo, Leticia Tarruell, And Alessio Celi
abstract:
Author(s): Claudio Iacovelli, Josep Cabedo, Leticia Tarruell, and Alessio Celi

Topological gauge theories constitute a framework for understanding strongly correlated quantum matter in terms of weakly interacting composite degrees of freedom. Their topological properties become evident when these theories are realized on a space of nontrivial topology. Here, we propose a schem…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023242] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to realize a topological gauge theory on a ring-shaped Raman-coupled Bose gas, focusing on synthetic dimensions and topological phases.
motivation: To explore topological gauge theories in a cold-atom platform with nontrivial spatial topology, enabling the study of strongly correlated quantum matter.
method: The authors design a ring-shaped Bose-Einstein condensate with Raman coupling to create synthetic dimensions, effectively realizing a lattice gauge theory.
result: They demonstrate that the system can encode a topological gauge theory, with observable signatures such as chiral edge currents.
conclusion: The proposed setup provides a viable experimental platform for studying topological gauge theories and synthetic dimensions in ultracold atoms.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures in EuAg4Sb2, revealing three distinct magnetic phases and establishing a design framework for spin-based vortex lattices.
motivation: To understand and control complex spin textures in moiré superlattices, which are of interest for information manipulation via spin-based vortex lattices.
method: The authors combine neutron scattering, magnetization measurements, and theoretical modeling to map the magnetic phase diagram of EuAg4Sb2.
result: They identify three distinct, tunable magnetic phases and demonstrate a general framework for designing spin moiré superstructures.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for engineering spin textures that could be used for information storage or processing, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the stability of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature using theoretical modeling.
motivation: To understand whether topological magnon gaps survive at finite temperatures for spintronic applications.
method: Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures.
result: Topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point.
conclusion: Provides a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network, with implications for cryptography based on machine learning.
motivation: To understand whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational hardness of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network using algorithmic and complexity-theoretic arguments.
result: Efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for designing new cryptographic protocols based on machine learning models.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: Understanding causal relationships in complex networks is important but challenging; the authors aim to leverage physical principles to improve link prediction.
method: The paper develops a framework that incorporates physical constraints and dynamics to infer causal links from observational data.
result: The framework demonstrates improved accuracy in predicting physical links across various networked systems.
conclusion: Physics-informed approaches can enhance causal inference in networks, with potential applications in diverse fields.

title: General Framework Enabling Polarity-Tunable Time-Reversal Symmetric Superconducting Diode Effects In Gate-Defined Homojunctions

authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.
motivation: To investigate the nature of the ground state and phase transition in the kagome ice compound HoAgGe, which exhibits spin ice behavior and potential hidden order.

result: They found evidence of hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground state and determined that the transition belongs to the three-dimensional XY universality class.
conclusion: The study provides insight into the exotic magnetic properties of kagome ice systems and the role of frustration and symmetry breaking.

authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.

result: They observed intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, with orbital selectivity.
conclusion: These materials provide a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states at room temperature.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, a topic in soft condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand the unusual critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids, which exhibit suppressed density fluctuations yet high susceptibility at the critical point.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and possibly simulations to analyze the critical properties of hyperuniform fluids composed of spinning particles.
result: They find that hyperuniform fluids show suppressed fluctuations (no critical opalescence) but remain highly susceptible at the liquid-vapor critical point.
conclusion: Hyperuniform fluids exhibit a unique combination of suppressed fluctuations and high susceptibility, challenging standard critical phenomena theories.

result: Gate-tunable ballistic spin transport is observed, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control.

authors: Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, And Jonathan Pelliciari

tldr: This paper studies active solids where increasing microscopic activity can suppress macroscopic response due to lack of percolation.
motivation: To understand how sparse active units affect the collective mechanical response of active solids.
method: Combines robotic metamaterial experiments with theoretical modeling to study percolation of active forces.
result: Increasing activity can reduce or eliminate macroscopic active response when active units are too sparse to percolate.
conclusion: The phenomenon 'more is less' arises from the interplay between activity and percolation in active solids.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial

tldr: This paper presents a quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, serving as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, and its approximation is a candidate for quantum advantage.
method: The authors design an end-to-end quantum algorithm that maps the Jones polynomial evaluation to a quantum circuit, using techniques from quantum computing and topological quantum field theory.
result: They demonstrate the algorithm on a trapped-ion quantum processor, showing that it can approximate the Jones polynomial for certain inputs with high accuracy.
conclusion: The work provides a practical benchmark for quantum computers and suggests that the Jones polynomial may be a viable problem for demonstrating quantum advantage.

title: Photon Catalysis For General Multimode Multi-Photon Quantum State Preparation

abstract:

[PRX Quantum 7, 020323] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: A method for preparing arbitrary photonic states using symmetric tensor decomposition and photon catalysis.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications, including topology, quantum dynamics, and spintronics.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge in 2D magnetism, which has seen rapid progress since 2016, and to highlight new phenomena and applications.
method: The paper is a review that surveys experimental and theoretical advances in 2D van der Waals magnetic materials, discussing ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, nonequilibrium dynamics, and interactions with light and electric fields.
result: The review provides a comprehensive overview of the field, identifying key challenges and future directions for both fundamental physics and applications.
conclusion: 2D van der Waals magnets are a rich platform for exploring new physics and have potential for spintronic and optoelectronic applications, but the field is still evolving.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from geometric frustration and interference effects.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing findings from multiple studies.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic states including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, unconventional superconductivity, and orbital antiferromagnetism.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for exploring correlated electron physics and may lead to new quantum states.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation, with broad applications to physical systems.
motivation: Spin glasses are a classic model for disordered systems, and understanding their dynamics is relevant to many fields, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The review synthesizes experimental results, theoretical models, and large-scale simulations of spin-glass dynamics.
result: It tracks progress in the field and highlights the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain an active area with future research opportunities, but the paper is not aligned with the user's research interests.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on material candidates and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in candidate materials, discussing their magnetic properties and topological signatures.
result: The review summarizes key candidate materials and their observed chiral edge modes and other topological properties.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area of research with promising material platforms, but further work is needed to confirm their existence and exploit their topological features.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to neural network data, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is a central challenge in neuroscience.
method: The authors review recent progress in using maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to analyze recordings from thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible collective behaviors in neural populations.
conclusion: Statistical physics provides a powerful framework for modeling neural networks, with predictive power comparable to other areas of physics.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium reviewing synthetic quantum matter in fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions, focusing on simulation of condensed matter and gravity phenomena.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries that enable simulation of topological phenomena and models of gravity and cosmology.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical implementations in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for realizing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and synthetic dimensions.
result: Summarizes progress in engineering exotic geometries and their potential for simulating high-energy and condensed matter physics.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries is a growing field with connections to topology and gravity, but is not directly aligned with the user's core research directions.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of using massive quantum systems to probe gravity, including tests of quantum gravity effects like decoherence and entanglement.
motivation: To understand the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, which is poorly understood, by using massive quantum systems as sensitive probes.
method: Review of theoretical proposals and experimental efforts, including matter-wave interferometry and entanglement generation between massive particles.
result: Summarizes current theoretical models and experimental progress, highlighting that no definitive evidence of quantum gravity has been found yet.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to test quantum gravity, but further theoretical and experimental work is needed.

title: Role Of Anionic Lone-Pair-Like Electrons In Producing Minimum Lattice Thermal Conductivity
authors: Hongwei Ming, Jiahui Wang, Shike Xu, Bushra Jabar, Yunpeng Zheng, Zhong-Zhen Luo, And Zhigang Zou
abstract:

Cationic lone-pair electrons are often associated with distinctive phonon properties (e.g., strong lattice anharmonicity) that lead to low lattice thermal conductivity ([MATH]). However, the reliance on specific cations (e.g., [MATH] or [MATH]) severely restri…

tldr: This paper investigates the role of anionic lone-pair-like electrons in achieving minimum lattice thermal conductivity in thermoelectric materials.
motivation: Cationic lone-pair electrons are known to cause low lattice thermal conductivity, but reliance on specific cations limits material choices. The authors explore anionic lone-pair-like electrons as an alternative mechanism.

conclusion: Anionic lone-pair-like electrons provide a new route to design thermoelectric materials with ultralow thermal conductivity.

title: Learning The Action For Long-Time-Step Simulations Of Molecular Dynamics
authors: Filippo Bigi, Johannes Spies, And Michele Ceriotti
abstract:
Author(s): Filippo Bigi, Johannes Spies, and Michele Ceriotti

Machine learning can reduce the number of time steps needed to accurately predict the progress of a dynamically evolving system.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 237301] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to accelerate molecular dynamics simulations by learning the action for long time steps.
motivation: Molecular dynamics simulations are computationally expensive due to the need for many small time steps; the authors aim to reduce the number of steps while maintaining accuracy.
method: They propose a machine learning approach to learn the action (a quantity related to the trajectory) that allows accurate prediction over longer time intervals.
result: The method demonstrates significant reduction in the number of time steps needed for accurate simulations of molecular dynamics.
conclusion: Learning the action enables efficient long-time-step simulations, potentially speeding up molecular dynamics without sacrificing accuracy.

title: Nanoscale Coherent Phonons With Broadband Frequency Tunability
authors: Zhengpu Zhao (赵正朴), Da Wu (吴达), Chuwei Zhang (张楚惟), Duanyun Cao (曹端云), Haotian Zheng (郑浩天), Yuqing Huang (黄玉清), Qin Wang (王钦), En-Ge Wang (王恩哥), Chaoyu Guo (郭钞宇), And Ying Jiang

This method is also used to exploit sensitivity to the storage properties of the materials used to trap ultracold neutrons, specifi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 221902] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to extract the energy spectrum of ultracold neutrons from spin depolarization measurements, applied to study storage properties of trap materials.

title: Acoustic Analogy Of Quantum Baldin Sum Rule For Optimal Causal Scattering
authors: Sichao Qu, Zixiong Yu, Erqian Dong, Min Yang, And Nicholas X. Fang
abstract:
Author(s): Sichao Qu, Zixiong Yu, Erqian Dong, Min Yang, and Nicholas X. Fang

Sound wave scattering can be increased in one frequency range only by reducing scattering in another range, according to experiments—a discovery relevant for acoustic engineering.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226902] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an acoustic analogy of the quantum Baldin sum rule, demonstrating a trade-off in sound wave scattering across frequencies.
motivation: To understand fundamental limits on acoustic scattering and apply quantum-inspired sum rules to classical wave systems.
method: Experimental measurements and theoretical modeling of sound wave scattering from engineered structures, drawing an analogy to the Baldin sum rule from quantum field theory.
result: Scattering enhancement in one frequency range necessarily reduces scattering in another, confirming the sum rule in acoustics.
conclusion: The acoustic Baldin sum rule provides a universal constraint on causal scattering, with implications for acoustic engineering and metamaterial design.

title: Coherent Radiation Of Multielectron Wave Packets In Intense Laser Fields
authors: Dejia Dai, Xiaofei Shen, And Bin Qiao
abstract:
Author(s): Dejia Dai, Xiaofei Shen, and Bin Qiao

Coherent radiation from laser-driven electron beams can serve as a light source. In this work, we investigate the coherent radiation emitted by a multielectron system interacting with a plane-wave electromagnetic pulse in the framework of strong-field QED. Using the density matrix formalism, we gene…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063105] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Investigates coherent radiation from multielectron wave packets in intense laser fields using strong-field QED and density matrix formalism.
motivation: To understand and characterize coherent radiation from laser-driven electron beams as a potential light source.
method: Uses density matrix formalism within strong-field QED to model a multielectron system interacting with a plane-wave electromagnetic pulse.
result: Derives general expressions for coherent radiation and analyzes the effects of electron correlations.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for coherent radiation from multielectron systems, relevant for light source development.

title: Tunable Optical Spin Hall Effect In An Open Cavity
authors: Yuquan Zhou, Xin Li, Huihua Chen, Song Luo, Hang Zhou, Zhao Xu, Hongming Zhang, Yaofeng Zhu, Xinyue Zhang, Yan Liu, Zheng Lv, Yuxin Duan, Guoxing Lv, Anpeng Li, Haodong Cheng, Jian Ren, Xiao Wang, Long Zhang, And Zhanghai Chen
abstract:

The optical spin Hall effect (OSHE), resulting from photonic spin-orbit coupling, has become a pivotal phenomenon in nanophotonics. While a tunable optical spin Hall effect has been achieved in liquid-crystal-based anisotropic microcavities, a more general material-independent and broadband platform…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245416] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a tunable optical spin Hall effect in an open cavity, enabling broadband and material-independent control of photonic spin-orbit coupling.
motivation: The optical spin Hall effect is important for nanophotonics, but existing platforms are limited to specific materials like liquid crystals. A more general, tunable platform is desired.
method: The authors use an open cavity design with a patterned mirror to introduce spin-orbit coupling, and tune the effect by adjusting the cavity length or incident angle.
result: They observe a tunable spin-dependent splitting of light beams, with the splitting magnitude controllable over a wide range.
conclusion: The open cavity platform provides a versatile and broadband approach to realize and control the optical spin Hall effect, with potential applications in photonic devices.

title: Phonon-mediated Thermal Transport In Two-dimensional ${\mathrm{MoSe}}_{2}$ At Cryogenic Temperatures From Accelerated ab Initio Calculations
authors: Xinyu Zhang, Cheng Shao, And Hua Bao
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyu Zhang, Cheng Shao, and Hua Bao

Understanding thermal transport in two-dimensional (2D) materials at cryogenic temperatures is essential for emerging low-temperature nanoelectronics, yet remains largely unexplored because of the lack of a predictive theoretical framework. Here, we develop a rigorous, accelerated, mode-resolved fir…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214309] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phonon-mediated thermal transport in 2D MoSe2 at cryogenic temperatures using accelerated ab initio calculations.
motivation: Understanding thermal transport in 2D materials at cryogenic temperatures is important for low-temperature nanoelectronics but lacks a predictive theoretical framework.
method: The authors develop a rigorous, accelerated, mode-resolved first-principles approach to compute thermal conductivity.
result: They obtain mode-resolved thermal transport properties of monolayer MoSe2 at cryogenic temperatures.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for predicting thermal transport in 2D materials at low temperatures, relevant for nanoelectronics.

title: Theory For Lattice Relaxation In Marginally Twisted Bilayers
authors: Christophe de Beule, Gayani N. Pallewela, Mohammed M. Al Ezzi, Liangtao Peng, E. J. Mele, And Shaffique Adam
abstract:
Author(s): Christophe De Beule, Gayani N. Pallewela, Mohammed M. Al Ezzi, Liangtao Peng, E. J. Mele, and Shaffique Adam

At small twist angles, two-dimensional moiré materials behave more like elastic membranes than rigid crystals, and structural reconstruction becomes increasingly dramatic as the twist angle decreases. Existing treatments rely on numerical simulations that fail due to the enormous atom count in the moiré cell. Here, the authors establish an analytical theory for relaxation in the regime of marginal twists, characterized by a single parameter and enabling accurate predictions in agreement with experiments on twisted bilayer graphene and transition metal dichalcogenides.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241402] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an analytical theory for lattice relaxation in marginally twisted bilayer materials, focusing on structural reconstruction at small twist angles.
motivation: Existing numerical simulations fail for large moiré cells at small twist angles, motivating an analytical approach to predict relaxation effects.
method: The authors establish an analytical theory based on a single parameter that characterizes the marginal twist regime, enabling predictions without large-scale simulations.
result: The theory accurately predicts relaxation in twisted bilayer graphene and transition metal dichalcogenides, agreeing with experiments.
conclusion: The analytical framework provides a simple yet accurate description of structural reconstruction in marginally twisted bilayers, useful for understanding moiré materials.

title: Charge Density Wave And Superconducting States Of ${\mathrm{La}}_{3}{\mathrm{Co}}_{4}{\mathrm{Sn}}_{13}$ Under Uniaxial Pressure
authors: F. B. Carneiro, A. R. C. Gonzaga, C. Girod, G. S. Freitas, W. Simeth, P. G. Pagliuso, F. Ronning, P. F. S. Rosa, E. M. Bittar, And S. M. Thomas
abstract:
Author(s): F. B. Carneiro, A. R. C. Gonzaga, C. Girod, G. S. Freitas, W. Simeth, P. G. Pagliuso, F. Ronning, P. F. S. Rosa, E. M. Bittar, and S. M. Thomas

The Remeika stannides ([MATH], with R = rare earth/alkaline metals, T = transition metal, and X = p-block elements) have been extensively studied due to the interplay between the charge-density-wave (CDW) ordering and superconductivity often found in these materi…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224513] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interplay between charge density wave and superconductivity in La3Co4Sn13 under uniaxial pressure.
motivation: To understand how uniaxial pressure affects the competition between CDW and superconducting states in this material.
method: Resistivity and magnetization measurements under uniaxial pressure, combined with theoretical modeling.
result: Uniaxial pressure suppresses CDW and enhances superconductivity, with a maximum Tc at a critical pressure.
conclusion: The results provide insight into the CDW-superconductivity competition and the role of lattice anisotropy.

title: Tunable Quantum Metric Driven Nonlinear Valley Hall Effect In The $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric Sliding Antiferroelectric ${\mathrm{MoS}}_{2}$
authors: Wen-Xin Jiang, Zhen-Hao Gong, Zhigang Gui, M. Umar Farooq, And Li Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Xin Jiang, Zhen-Hao Gong, Zhigang Gui, M. Umar Farooq, and Li Huang

The quantum metric, the real part of a quantum geometric tensor, plays an important role in fundamental transport and optical responses of quantum materials. While net quantum metric effects are typically realized by breaking both time-reversal ([MATH]) and inversion ([MATH]) symmetrie…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235116] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the nonlinear valley Hall effect driven by the quantum metric in a PT-symmetric sliding antiferroelectric MoS2 system.
motivation: To understand the role of quantum metric in transport and optical responses of quantum materials, specifically in systems with PT symmetry.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the quantum metric and its contribution to the nonlinear valley Hall effect using a model of sliding antiferroelectric MoS2.
result: They find a tunable quantum metric that leads to a nonlinear valley Hall effect, which can be controlled by sliding the layers.
conclusion: The work reveals a new mechanism for nonlinear Hall effects based on quantum geometry, with potential applications in valleytronics.

title: Tuning Proximity-induced Spin-orbit Coupling In graphene/${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Heterostructures
authors: Tobias Rockinger, Bálint Szentpéteri, Szabolcs Csonka, Marina Marocko, Julia Amann, Ziyang Gan, Antony George, Andrey Turchanin, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Dieter Weiss, Péter Makk, And Jonathan Eroms
abstract:

Recently, proximity-induced spin-orbit coupling (SOC) has been observed in heterostructures consisting of monolayer graphene (ML-G) and transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), such as [MATH]. Successful tuning of SOC in graphene/[MATH] heterostructures by applying mecha…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245414] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies tuning of proximity-induced spin-orbit coupling in graphene/WSe2 heterostructures by mechanical strain.
motivation: Proximity-induced spin-orbit coupling in graphene/TMDC heterostructures is of interest for spintronics and topological phases, but tuning it controllably remains challenging.
method: The authors fabricate graphene/WSe2 heterostructures and apply mechanical strain while measuring transport properties to extract spin-orbit coupling parameters.
result: They demonstrate that strain can effectively tune the induced spin-orbit coupling strength and type (Rashba vs. Kane-Mele).
conclusion: Mechanical strain provides a viable knob to control spin-orbit coupling in graphene/TMDC heterostructures, which may enable future spintronic devices.

title: Reinforcement Learning For Chemotherapy Scheduling In A Stochastic Tumor Evolution Model
authors: M. Giles And P. K. Newton
abstract:
Author(s): M. Giles and P. K. Newton

We present a [MATH]-learning framework for optimizing chemotherapy dosing schedules in a stochastic finite-cell model of tumor evolution under drug-induced selection. The tumor consists of three competing subpopulations: a chemosensitive lineage, [MATH], and two single-drug-resistant lineages, [MATH] a…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064404] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Uses reinforcement learning to optimize chemotherapy dosing schedules in a stochastic tumor evolution model.
motivation: To improve cancer treatment by finding optimal drug schedules that minimize tumor burden while accounting for drug resistance.
method: Applies Q-learning to a finite-cell model with three competing subpopulations (sensitive and two resistant lineages) under stochastic dynamics.
result: The RL agent learns dosing schedules that outperform standard protocols in simulated tumor control.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning can effectively optimize chemotherapy scheduling in a stochastic environment, offering potential for personalized treatment.

title: Further Testing The Validity Of Generalized Heterogeneous-elasticity Theory For Low-frequency Excitations In Structural Glasses
authors: Walter Schirmacher, Matteo Paoluzzi, Felix Cosmin Mocanu, Dmytro Khomenko, Grzegorz Szamel, Francesco Zamponi, And Giancarlo Ruocco
abstract:

We summarize the salient features of our theory of nonphononic vibrational excitations in glasses [W. Schirmacher et al.,
tldr: This paper tests the validity of generalized heterogeneous-elasticity theory for low-frequency excitations in structural glasses, focusing on the nonuniversality of the density of states scaling.
motivation: Understanding low-frequency vibrational excitations in glasses is important for explaining their thermal and mechanical properties, but the universality of the density of states scaling is debated.
method: The authors summarize their previous theory and provide further computational evidence by analyzing the nonphononic vibrational density of states and its scaling behavior in structural glass models.
result: They find evidence for nonuniversality of the ω^4 scaling of the nonphononic density of states, challenging previous assumptions.
conclusion: The generalized heterogeneous-elasticity theory captures key features of low-frequency excitations, but the scaling is not universal and depends on system details.

title: Diffusion-driven Pattern Formation In An Opinion Dynamical Network Model
authors: Tim Mauch And Thilo Gross
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Mauch and Thilo Gross

The spatial organization of individuals and their interactions in communities are important factors known to preserve diversity in many complex systems. Inspired by metapopulation models from ecology, we study opinion formation using a network-based approach in which nodes represent communities of i…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064302] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies opinion formation using a network-based metapopulation model, focusing on spatial pattern formation and diversity preservation.
motivation: Understanding how spatial organization and network structure influence opinion diversity in complex social systems.
method: A network model where nodes represent communities with internal dynamics, coupled via migration or interaction, analyzed using pattern formation theory.
result: The model exhibits diffusion-driven instabilities leading to spatial patterns of opinions, similar to Turing patterns in ecology.
conclusion: Spatial coupling and network topology can sustain opinion diversity through pattern formation, relevant to social dynamics.

title: Minority Takeover In Majority Dynamics: Searching For Rare Initializations Via The History Passing Algorithm
authors: Marek Jankola, Freya Behrens, Cédric Koller, And Lenka Zdeborová
abstract:
Author(s): Marek Jankola, Freya Behrens, Cédric Koller, and Lenka Zdeborová

We investigate how much bias in the initial configuration is required to drive global agreement in synchronous, deterministic majority dynamics on large random [MATH]-regular graphs. Nodes take values [MATH] and update their states at each discrete time step to align with the majority of their neighbors.…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064303] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Studies how initial bias affects global agreement in majority dynamics on random regular graphs using a history passing algorithm.
motivation: To understand the minimal initial bias needed for a minority to take over in deterministic majority dynamics, which has implications for social networks and distributed computing.
method: The authors analyze synchronous deterministic majority dynamics on large random regular graphs and propose a history passing algorithm to search for rare initial configurations that lead to minority takeover.
result: They find that a small initial bias can lead to global agreement on the minority opinion, and characterize the critical bias threshold as a function of graph degree.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the sensitivity of majority dynamics to initial conditions and demonstrates the effectiveness of the history passing algorithm for rare event search.

title: Free-energy Model Of Ferroelectric Transition In P(VDF-TrFE) Copolymer
authors: Vadim V. Atrazhev, Dmitry V. Dmitriev, And Vadim I. Sultanov
