We develop a physics-based analytical model for the ferroelectric-to-paraelectric phase transition in poly(vinylidene difluoride-co-trifluoroethylene) [P(VDF-TrFE)] copolymers. The low-temperature ferroelectric phase is an orthorhombic crystal analogous to the poly(vinylidene difluoride) β-phase, wh…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065405] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Develops a free-energy model for the ferroelectric-to-paraelectric phase transition in P(VDF-TrFE) copolymers.
motivation: To understand the phase transition mechanism in a technologically relevant ferroelectric polymer.
method: Constructs a physics-based analytical free-energy model incorporating dipole interactions and chain conformations.
result: The model reproduces the temperature dependence of polarization and transition temperature, matching experimental data.
conclusion: The model provides a quantitative description of the ferroelectric transition in P(VDF-TrFE) copolymers.

title: Externally Driven Condensates Show Translation-induced Polarization, Directed Coalescence, And Anomalous Diffusion In Viscoelastic Media
authors: Andriy Goychuk
abstract:
Author(s): Andriy Goychuk

Phase separation into compositionally and physically distinct domains is ubiquitous in (non)living matter ranging from alloys and emulsions to biomolecular condensates in cells. The organization of these domains can be controlled, for example, by nonequilibrium chemical reactions, external fields, o…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065402] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phase separation in externally driven condensates in viscoelastic media, focusing on polarization, coalescence, and anomalous diffusion.
motivation: Understanding how external driving and viscoelasticity affect the dynamics and organization of phase-separated domains in soft matter.
method: Theoretical modeling and numerical simulations of condensate dynamics under external fields in a viscoelastic medium.
result: External driving induces translation-induced polarization, directed coalescence, and anomalous diffusion of condensates.
conclusion: External fields and viscoelasticity can control condensate organization, with implications for biological and soft matter systems.

title: First-passage-time Properties Of Diffusion With A Broad Class Of Stochastic Diffusion Coefficients
authors: Go Uchida, Hiromi Miyoshi, And Hitoshi Washizu
abstract:
Author(s): Go Uchida, Hiromi Miyoshi, and Hitoshi Washizu

This study investigates the first-passage-time (FPT) properties of particles with a broad class of positive stochastic diffusion coefficients (DCs), representing diffusion in heterogeneous environments or of particles with conformational fluctuations. We demonstrate that for diffusion in a one-dimen…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064108] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage-time properties of diffusion with stochastic diffusion coefficients in heterogeneous environments.
motivation: Understanding first-passage times in heterogeneous media is important for transport in disordered systems and biological processes.
method: Analytical and numerical methods are used to derive FPT distributions for a broad class of positive stochastic diffusion coefficients in one dimension.
result: The FPT properties depend on the statistics of the diffusion coefficient, with explicit expressions for certain cases.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for analyzing diffusion in fluctuating environments, but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Unveiling Dielectric Relaxation And Shear Rheology In Water
authors: Songming Liu And Jiaxing Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): Songming Liu and Jiaxing Yuan

The complex dynamics of liquid water are manifested in its unique dielectric relaxation and nonlinear shear rheology. We investigate the dielectric and rheological responses of TIP4P/[MATH] water using molecular dynamics simulations across a wide temperature range, including the deeply supercooled regi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023266] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Molecular dynamics study of dielectric relaxation and shear rheology in water using TIP4P model.
motivation: To understand the complex dynamics of liquid water, especially in the deeply supercooled regime.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations of TIP4P water across a wide temperature range.
result: Characterization of dielectric and rheological responses.
conclusion: Provides insights into water's relaxation and mechanical properties.

title: Trapping And Cooling Mechanisms In Blue-detuned Magneto-optical Traps Of Molecules
authors: Qinshu Lyu And M. R. Tarbutt
abstract:
Author(s): Qinshu Lyu and M. R. Tarbutt

This work identifies the mechanisms responsible for trapping and cooling in a blue-detuned magneto-optical trap driven by a pair of closely spaced frequency components of opposite circular polarization. When the Zeeman splitting matches the frequency difference between the two components, there is a state that is dark to the beam propagating in one direction but not to the beam from the opposite direction, generating a radiation pressure force toward the field zero.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023259] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies trapping and cooling mechanisms in blue-detuned magneto-optical traps for molecules, focusing on radiation pressure forces from two-frequency components.
motivation: Understanding and improving laser cooling and trapping of molecules is important for precision measurements and quantum science, but the paper is primarily an atomic/molecular physics study.
method: The authors analyze a blue-detuned magneto-optical trap using two closely spaced frequency components with opposite circular polarization, and identify a dark state mechanism that generates a radiation pressure force toward the field zero.
result: They identify the trapping and cooling mechanisms, showing how Zeeman splitting matching the frequency difference creates direction-dependent dark states that produce a confining force.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical understanding of blue-detuned MOTs for molecules, which may aid in developing new cooling schemes.

title: Quantum-enhanced T-stochastic Neighbor Embedding For High-dimensional Data Visualization
authors: Xin Zhang, Chao-Hua Yu, Gong-De Guo, And Song Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Xin Zhang, Chao-Hua Yu, Gong-De Guo, and Song Lin

t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) is a nonlinear dimensionality reduction algorithm that preserves local similarity by matching probability distributions between high- and low-dimensional spaces. Owing to its ability to capture complex manifold structures, t-SNE has become a widely…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023265] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum-enhanced version of t-SNE for high-dimensional data visualization using quantum amplitude estimation and Grover's search.
motivation: Classical t-SNE is computationally expensive for large datasets; quantum algorithms may offer speedup.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that estimates probability distributions and performs gradient descent using quantum subroutines.
result: The quantum t-SNE achieves quadratic speedup in certain steps compared to classical t-SNE.
conclusion: Quantum computing can accelerate nonlinear dimensionality reduction, but practical implementation remains challenging.

title: Dynamic Similarity Of Vortex Shedding In A Superfluid Flowing Past A Penetrable Obstacle
authors: Junhwan Kwon And Yong-Il Shin
abstract:
Author(s): Junhwan Kwon and Yong-il Shin

We numerically investigate wake dynamics in a superfluid flowing past a penetrable obstacle. The penetrable obstacle does not fully deplete the density, and we define an effective diameter [MATH] from the Mach-1 contour of the time-averaged irrotational flow around the obstacle, which …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023246] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Numerical study of vortex shedding dynamics in a superfluid flowing past a penetrable obstacle, focusing on dynamic similarity and effective diameter definition.
motivation: To understand wake dynamics in superfluids with penetrable obstacles, which are relevant to quantum turbulence and superfluid hydrodynamics.
method: Numerical simulations of the Gross-Pitaevskii equation for a superfluid flow past a penetrable obstacle, analyzing vortex shedding patterns and defining an effective diameter from the Mach-1 contour.
result: The vortex shedding frequency scales with the effective diameter, showing dynamic similarity analogous to classical fluids.
conclusion: Penetrable obstacles in superfluids exhibit vortex shedding with dynamic similarity, extending classical fluid dynamics concepts to quantum fluids.

title: Reducibility Of Higher-order To Pairwise Interactions: Social Impact Models On Hypergraphs
authors: Jaume Llabrés, Raúl Toral, Maxi San Miguel, And Federico Vázquez
abstract:
Author(s): Jaume Llabrés, Raúl Toral, Maxi San Miguel, and Federico Vázquez

We show that a general class of node-update social impact models with higher-order interactions on hypergraphs can be exactly mapped to an equivalent model with pairwise interactions on a weighted projected network. This mapping preserves the microscopic probabilities of changing the state of the no…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023250] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that a class of social impact models with higher-order interactions on hypergraphs can be exactly reduced to pairwise interactions on a weighted projected network.
motivation: Higher-order interactions are common in social systems, but analyzing hypergraph models is complex. The authors aim to simplify such models by mapping them to pairwise interactions.
method: They prove an exact mapping from a general class of node-update social impact models on hypergraphs to equivalent models with pairwise interactions on a weighted projected network, preserving microscopic transition probabilities.
result: The mapping is exact for the considered class of models, enabling the use of standard network analysis tools for hypergraph-based social dynamics.
conclusion: Higher-order interactions in these social impact models can be effectively captured by pairwise interactions with appropriate weights, simplifying analysis without loss of accuracy.

title: Multiobjective Tweezers In Scattering Media
authors: Tristan Nerson, Jakob Hüpfl, Clément Ferise, David Globosits, Marlene Hudler, Matthieu Malléjac, Stefan Rotter, And Romain Fleury
abstract:

Radiation forces and torques enable the manipulation of objects with acoustic and electromagnetic waves. Yet, harnessing them in complex scattering media remains a formidable challenge, especially when multiple objects must be controlled under competing objectives. Here, we demonstrate that sound or…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023254] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates multi-objective manipulation of particles using acoustic tweezers in complex scattering media.
motivation: Controlling multiple objects with radiation forces in scattering environments is challenging; the authors aim to achieve simultaneous manipulation under competing objectives.
method: They use wavefront shaping and optimization algorithms to generate acoustic fields that trap and move multiple particles independently in a scattering medium.
result: Experimental and numerical results show successful independent control of multiple particles, even in highly scattering environments.
conclusion: Multiobjective tweezers enable complex particle manipulation in scattering media, with potential applications in biophysics and microfluidics.

title: Compression, Simulation, And Synthesis Of Turbulent Flows With Tensor Trains

tldr: This paper applies tensor train decompositions to compress, simulate, and synthesize turbulent fluid flows, demonstrating computational speedups.
motivation: Turbulent flow simulations are computationally expensive due to high spatial resolution requirements; tensor methods offer a way to reduce complexity.
method: The authors use tensor train (TT) decompositions to represent turbulent flow data and dynamics, enabling efficient compression and simulation.
result: The TT-based approach achieves significant compression ratios and accelerates numerical simulations while maintaining accuracy.
conclusion: Tensor trains are a promising tool for large-scale turbulence simulations, reducing computational cost without sacrificing fidelity.

title: Phenomenology Of Orbital Torque, Pumping, And Mixing Conductance In Metallic Bilayers

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023239] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A phenomenological model for orbital torque and pumping in metallic bilayers, focusing on spin-orbit conversion in light metals.
motivation: To understand the conversion between spin and orbital currents in magnetic bilayers, which is relevant for spintronics.
method: Develops a phenomenological model based on diffusion equations and boundary conditions to describe orbital torque and pumping.
result: Derives expressions for orbital torque, pumping, and mixing conductance, showing that orbital transport can be described analogously to spin transport.
conclusion: The model provides a framework for interpreting experiments on orbital torque and may guide material design for spintronic applications.

title: Intertwined Polar, Chiral, And Ferro-Rotational Orders In A Homo-Ferro-Rotational Insulator
authors: Weizhe Zhang, June Ho Yeo, Xiaoyu Guo, Tony Chiang, Nishkarsh Agarwal, John T. Heron, Kai Sun, Junjie Yang, Sang-Wook Cheong, Youngjun Ahn, And Liuyan Zhao

Multimodal optical characterization of Ni
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021030] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of intertwined polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational orders in a bulk insulator using multimodal optical characterization.
motivation: To understand the coupling between multiple ferroic orders and the formation of complex domain walls in a material with a uniform ferro-rotational state.
method: Multimodal optical characterization techniques, including second harmonic generation and optical anisotropy measurements, were used to probe the structural and electronic properties of Ni₃TeO₆.
result: The study identifies a uniform ferro-rotational state that couples polarity and chirality, leading to complex mixed-type domain walls.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new type of multiferroic order with intertwined polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational degrees of freedom, which may have implications for functional materials.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman

tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in disordered stealthy hyperuniform photonic crystals, revealing unexpected residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show residual scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale experiments on silicon photonic crystals combined with theoretical modeling to analyze scattering and radiative loss.
result: Unexpected residual scattering is driven by radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of near-perfect transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight limitations of stealthy hyperuniformity for photonic applications and suggest design modifications.

title: Dipolar Nematic State In Relaxor Ferroelectrics
authors: Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, And Shi Liu

motivation: Relaxor ferroelectrics exhibit complex ordering; understanding the dipolar nematic state is important for fundamental physics and potential applications.
method: The authors likely use experimental techniques (e.g., neutron scattering, dielectric spectroscopy) and theoretical modeling to characterize the nematic ordering.
result: A dipolar nematic state is identified in relaxor ferroelectrics, revealing a new type of ordering.

title: Nearly Isotropic Upper Critical Field In Pressurized Trilayer Nickelate ${\mathrm{La}}_{4}{\mathrm{Ni}}_{3}{\mathrm{O}}_{10−δ}$
authors: Di Peng et Al.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: A review of radiation forces and torques in optics and acoustics, focusing on momentum and spin densities.
motivation: To provide a unified perspective on how wave fields exert forces and torques on particles, with applications in trapping, sorting, and manipulation.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and experimental demonstrations of optical and acoustic radiation forces and torques.
result: It summarizes key concepts like local energy, momentum, and spin densities, and their role in generating forces and torques.
conclusion: The review highlights the broad applicability of radiation forces in particle manipulation across optics and acoustics.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and their applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key photophysical process affecting the efficiency of light-emitting devices and solar energy conversion, yet its theoretical description remains challenging.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models, including Fermi's golden rule, nonadiabatic coupling, and mixed quantum-classical dynamics, to describe internal conversion.
result: The review summarizes the strengths and limitations of current methods and identifies open questions in the field.
conclusion: Improved theoretical methods for internal conversion are needed to better predict and optimize photophysical properties in applications like photonics and energy harvesting.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, including possible mediators and connections to dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to probe fundamental discrete symmetries through spin-dependent forces.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models of exotic boson-mediated spin-dependent interactions and surveys experimental techniques such as atomic magnetometry, torsion balances, and precision spectroscopy.
result: Summarizes current constraints on coupling constants and mass ranges for various exotic bosons, and identifies promising future experimental directions.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain a vibrant field with many open questions; further experimental and theoretical work is needed to discover or constrain new physics.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in polar active matter, focusing on collective motion in biological and soft matter systems.
motivation: To understand how self-alignment of active units with their velocity leads to novel collective behaviors, with applications in biology, smart materials, and robotics.
method: The paper reviews existing models and experiments on self-alignment in active matter, presenting a unified mathematical framework.
result: Self-alignment enables phenomena such as orbiting in harmonic traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies, distinct from neighbor-based alignment.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a fundamental mechanism in active matter that can be harnessed for designing new materials and robotic systems.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on surface defects, electric fields, and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-voltage devices; understanding its mechanism is crucial for improving reliability.
method: The authors synthesize experimental observations and computer simulations to build a coherent mechanistic picture of the breakdown process.
result: A multi-step model involving surface defects, electrical stress, heating, and particle emission explains the onset of vacuum arcs.
conclusion: Improved understanding can lead to better design of accelerator structures and other high-power technologies.

This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational waves and X-ray pulse profiles.
motivation: Neutron stars are the densest objects in the universe, and their properties provide crucial tests of nuclear physics under extreme conditions.
method: The paper reviews recent gravitational-wave detections from binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile measurements, comparing them to theoretical predictions of the nuclear equation of state.
result: Observations constrain neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, which are compared to extrapolations of nuclear equation of state models.
conclusion: Future observations will further refine our understanding of dense matter, but the paper does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the paper reviews three real-space techniques to address this challenge.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, highlighting cases where techniques are combined.
result: The review demonstrates that these techniques can directly access atomic-scale disorder information, especially when used in combination.
conclusion: Combined real-space microscopy methods provide a more complete picture of defects in semiconductors, aiding materials science.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: A review of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonances.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions in stars is crucial for stellar burning and element formation, but many reactions are difficult to measure directly.
method: Summarizes theoretical approaches including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discusses experimental techniques.
result: Provides a comprehensive overview of the state of the art in low-energy nuclear reaction theory.
conclusion: The review highlights the importance of quantum phenomena in stellar nucleosynthesis and suggests new experimental approaches.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser-induced ultrasound to image deep tissues with optical contrast.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed to provide biological and clinical insight into cells and tissues, particularly for deep-tissue imaging with high resolution.

The description of the electronic structure in terms of extended Bloch states has made it possible to understand and calculate many properties in condensed-matter physics. However, understanding and insight often require a local description, and Wannier functions provide an exact and insightful map of extended reciprocal-space Bloch states into localized real-space orbitals. Applications range far and wide, from ultra-accurate integrations to topological invariants, and their widespread uptake by the electronic-structure community has resulted in a growing and interoperable ecosystem of methods and associated software tools. This review provides a description of this ecosystem that has now become a major instrument for the electronic-structure community in its pursuit of understanding, discovering, and designing materials.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045008] Published Mon Dec 23, 2024.
tldr: A review of the Wannier-function software ecosystem for materials simulations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the methods and tools based on Wannier functions for electronic structure calculations.
method: The paper surveys various software packages and their interoperability, focusing on the generation and use of maximally localized Wannier functions.
result: It describes the ecosystem's capabilities for computing band structures, topological invariants, and other material properties.
conclusion: The Wannier-function approach is a powerful and widely used tool in condensed-matter physics, with a mature software ecosystem.

However, satellites regularly observe solitary potential structures in space plasmas that are isolated positive or negative potential humps, called electron or ion holes. In the 1970s, laboratory observations were made of electron holes. This review presents an overview of the observation of these electrostatic structures and presents their origin and their stability, using analytic theory and simulations. The role of kinetically unstable velocity distributions is identified as a key driver.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045007] Published Tue Dec 10, 2024.
tldr: A review of solitary electrostatic structures (phase-space holes) in collisionless plasma, covering observations, theory, and simulations.
motivation: To understand the origin and stability of isolated potential humps observed in space plasmas, which are not explained by standard quasineutral plasma theory.
method: Review of satellite observations, laboratory experiments, analytic theory, and particle-in-cell simulations of electron and ion holes.
result: Phase-space holes arise from kinetic instabilities in velocity distributions and can be stable over long times, explaining many space plasma observations.
conclusion: Kinetic solitary structures are a fundamental nonlinear phenomenon in collisionless plasmas, with implications for space weather and plasma diagnostics.

Enrichment is observed, with broad implications for foam stability, transport phenomena, and applications.

#SoftMatterSpotlight


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L063401] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies surfactant concentration profiles in liquid foams using neutron scattering, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding surfactant distribution in foams is important for foam stability and applications, but the topic is classical soft matter physics.
method: Small-angle neutron scattering with contrast matching, combined with optical and electrical probes, was used to measure surfactant concentration profiles.
result: Enrichment of surfactant concentration was observed in the foam.
conclusion: The findings have implications for foam stability and transport phenomena, but are unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Collective Dynamics Of Natural Killer Cells Interacting With Cancer And Fibroblast Cells
authors: Yun-Xuan Zhang, Shu-Chen Liu, And Lin I
abstract:
Author(s): Yun-Xuan Zhang, Shu-Chen Liu, and Lin I

The authors tested the response of natural killer cells cocultured with cancer cells and with fibroblasts. They found that natural killer cells targeted the cancer cells, but not fibroblasts. The natural killer cells clustered around cancer cells and promoted apoptosis, whereas they scouted around fibroblasts and did not form large aggregates. Generality of these responses could be established by testing additional normal cell types and tumor lines.

#BiophysicsSpotlight #BroadlyAccessible #Interdisciplinary


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062401] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the collective dynamics of natural killer cells interacting with cancer and fibroblast cells, a topic in cellular biophysics.
motivation: To understand how natural killer cells distinguish between cancer cells and normal fibroblasts, and how their collective behavior differs.
method: Coculture experiments of natural killer cells with cancer cells and fibroblasts, observing clustering and apoptosis.
result: Natural killer cells cluster around cancer cells and promote apoptosis, but scout around fibroblasts without forming aggregates.
conclusion: The response is specific to cancer cells, suggesting a general mechanism for immune surveillance.

title: Sea-surface Retention Effect Shapes Ocean Microplastic Fibers
authors: Andrea Mazzino And Giuseppe Suaria
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Mazzino and Giuseppe Suaria

Microfibers contaminate the global ocean, but their impact depends on length-dependent residence at the air-sea interface. In the submillimeter range, the sea surface exhibits a surface-enrichment signature: The long-to-short fiber ratio is higher at the interface than a few meters below (about 5 m)…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023283] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the retention of microplastic fibers at the sea surface, finding that longer fibers are enriched at the air-sea interface compared to subsurface waters.
motivation: Microplastic fibers are a major pollutant in the ocean, but their vertical distribution and residence time at the surface are poorly understood, which affects their environmental impact.
method: The authors combine field measurements of fiber length distributions at the sea surface and at 5 m depth with a theoretical model of fiber rise velocity and turbulent mixing.
result: They observe a higher ratio of long to short fibers at the surface than at depth, indicating a surface-enrichment effect that depends on fiber length.
conclusion: The sea surface selectively retains longer microplastic fibers, which has implications for their transport, degradation, and ingestion by marine organisms.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of Dephasing Reduction In An Optically Guided Laser-plasma Accelerator
authors: Ronan Lahaye, Igor A. Andriyash, Julien Gautier, Olena Kononenko, Adrien Leblanc, Jean-Philippe Goddet, Amar Tafzi, And Cédric Thaury
abstract:
Author(s): Ronan Lahaye, Igor A. Andriyash, Julien Gautier, Olena Kononenko, Adrien Leblanc, Jean-Philippe Goddet, Amar Tafzi, and Cédric Thaury

Laser-plasma accelerators offer a compact means of producing high-energy electron beams, but their performance is fundamentally limited by dephasing between the accelerated electrons and the plasma wave. To overcome this limitation, we investigate the combination of plasma density tapering and optic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023274] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates dephasing reduction in a laser-plasma accelerator using plasma density tapering and optical guiding.
motivation: Laser-plasma accelerators are limited by dephasing between electrons and the plasma wave; the authors aim to overcome this to improve electron beam energy and quality.
method: They experimentally combine plasma density tapering with optical guiding to extend the acceleration length and reduce dephasing.
result: The technique successfully reduces dephasing, leading to higher-energy electron beams with improved stability.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical path to enhance the performance of laser-plasma accelerators for compact high-energy applications.

title: Generation Of Attosecond Pulses From Relativistic Oscillating Plasma Gratings
authors: Hao-Jie Zhang, Bo-Yuan Li, Xiang-Yan An, Rong Huang, Zheng-Ming Sheng, Feng Liu, And Min Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Hao-Jie Zhang, Bo-Yuan Li, Xiang-Yan An, Rong Huang, Zheng-Ming Sheng, Feng Liu, and Min Chen

We propose a scheme to generate two isolated attosecond pulses at controllable angles through the interaction between relativistic laser pulses and a solid target. Two [MATH]-polarized laser pulses with certain frequency chirps are employed to drive oscillating plasma gratings (OPGs) on the target surf…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023261] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to generate attosecond pulses using relativistic oscillating plasma gratings driven by chirped laser pulses.
motivation: Attosecond pulse generation is important for ultrafast science, and the authors aim to produce isolated attosecond pulses at controllable angles.
method: Two chirped laser pulses interact with a solid target to create oscillating plasma gratings, which reflect the pulses to generate attosecond bursts.
result: The scheme yields two isolated attosecond pulses with controllable emission angles.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a new way to generate attosecond pulses with angular control, relevant to ultrafast optics and plasma physics.

title: Unified Model For Full-stage Shear Thickening Via Surface Chemistry And Friction
authors: Kang Wang, Bing Liu, Quan Liu, Huaxia Deng, And Xinglong Gong
abstract:
Author(s): Kang Wang, Bing Liu, Quan Liu, Huaxia Deng, and Xinglong Gong

Shear thickening fluid exhibits complex properties in a wide range of external conditions, leading to the significance for probing its state-transition property at the molecular level. Here, we propose a constitutive model that unifies the three rheological stages of shear thinning, shear thickening…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023263] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a constitutive model for shear thickening fluids based on surface chemistry and friction, unifying three rheological stages.
motivation: Shear thickening fluids exhibit complex state-transition properties under varying external conditions, and understanding these at the molecular level is important for applications.
method: The authors develop a constitutive model that incorporates surface chemistry and friction effects to describe shear thinning, shear thickening, and the transition between them.
result: The model successfully unifies the three rheological stages and matches experimental data.
conclusion: The proposed model provides a molecular-level understanding of shear thickening behavior, which could aid in designing smart materials.

title: Inhibitory Synaptic Timescales Drive Oscillatory Regime Transitions In Recurrent Excitatory-inhibitory Networks
authors: Siamak Kheiri, Saeed Taghavi, Matjaž Perc, And Alireza Valizadeh
abstract:
Author(s): Siamak Kheiri, Saeed Taghavi, Matjaž Perc, and Alireza Valizadeh

In recurrent cortical networks, inhibitory kinetics are often assumed to tune oscillation frequency continuously. Using a recurrent excitatory-inhibitory (E-I) model with fixed excitatory synaptic dynamics, we systematically vary inhibitory decay time constants and show instead that inhibitory times…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023251] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how inhibitory synaptic timescales drive oscillatory regime transitions in recurrent excitatory-inhibitory networks, a topic in computational neuroscience.
motivation: Understanding how inhibitory kinetics shape network oscillations is important for modeling cortical dynamics.
method: The authors systematically vary inhibitory decay time constants in a recurrent E-I model with fixed excitatory dynamics.
result: They find that inhibitory timescales can cause abrupt transitions between oscillatory regimes, rather than continuous frequency tuning.
conclusion: Inhibitory kinetics play a critical role in determining network oscillation patterns, with implications for neural information processing.

title: Comment On “Experimental Demonstration Of Electric Power Generation From Earth's Rotation Through Its Own Magnetic Field”
authors: Rinke J. Wijngaarden
abstract:
Author(s): Rinke J. Wijngaarden

In a recent paper, Chyba et al. [
tldr: This comment refutes a claim of generating electric power from Earth's rotation using a stationary device, showing it violates fundamental physics.
motivation: To correct a published claim that appears to violate conservation laws and basic electromagnetism.
method: The author analyzes the proposed device using Maxwell's equations and the principle of motional EMF, showing no net voltage is generated.
result: The claimed power generation is impossible because the device is stationary relative to Earth's magnetic field, and any induced EMF cancels out.
conclusion: The original paper's conclusion is incorrect; no net power can be extracted from Earth's rotation by a stationary device.

title: Super-resonance: Breaking The Bandwidth Limit Of Resonant Modes And Its Application To Flow Control
authors: Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, And Mahmoud I. Hussein
abstract:
Author(s): Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, and Mahmoud I. Hussein

Super-resonance maintains a broadband out-of-phase response well beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling broadband flow stabilization among other applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021045] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces super-resonance, a phenomenon that breaks the bandwidth limit of resonant modes, and applies it to flow control.
motivation: Conventional resonance has a limited bandwidth, which restricts its application in areas like flow control. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally demonstrate super-resonance, achieving a broadband out-of-phase response beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance.
result: Super-resonance enables broadband flow stabilization and other applications by maintaining a broadband out-of-phase response.
conclusion: Super-resonance breaks the bandwidth limit of resonant modes, offering new possibilities for flow control and potentially other fields.

title: Using Folded Proteins As Mechanically Well-Defined Units To Understand Fatigue Fracture In Hydrogels: Bridging Single Molecule And Bulk Studies
authors: Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, And Hai Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, and Hai Lei

A force-response model helps understand fatigue behavior and provides a design strategy for fatigue resistant hydrogels and soft materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021031] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fatigue fracture in hydrogels using folded proteins as mechanically well-defined units, bridging single-molecule and bulk experiments.
motivation: Understanding fatigue fracture in soft materials is crucial for designing durable hydrogels, but the molecular mechanisms are poorly understood.
method: The authors use folded proteins as model units to probe mechanical fatigue at the single-molecule level and develop a force-response model to connect single-molecule behavior to bulk fatigue properties.
result: They identify key molecular determinants of fatigue and propose design strategies for fatigue-resistant hydrogels.
conclusion: The work provides a mechanistic understanding of fatigue in hydrogels and offers a design principle for improving their durability.

title: Hydroplasticity Of Nanocrystal Films Induced By Mesopore Change
authors: Siyuan Liu, Yonggui Wang, Yu Yin, Xintong Meng, Zhen Lang, And Kai Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siyuan Liu, Yonggui Wang, Yu Yin, Xintong Meng, Zhen Lang, and Kai Zhang

A vapor training process allows for improved plasticity and better shaping of wood-derived films.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021026] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the hydroplasticity of nanocrystal films induced by mesopore change, focusing on wood-derived films and vapor training.
motivation: To improve the plasticity and shaping of wood-derived films for practical applications.
method: A vapor training process is used to induce mesopore changes in nanocrystal films.
result: The process leads to improved plasticity and better shaping of the films.
conclusion: The vapor training method effectively enhances the mechanical properties of wood-derived nanocrystal films.

title: Tracking Ultrafast Ion Diffusion Dynamics In ${\mathrm{AgCrSe}}_{2}$ Superionic Conductor
authors: Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, And Jiaqing He

Author(s): Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, and Jiaqing He

Direct spatial and temporal characterization of ion diffusion in superionic conductors provides a better link to macroscopic properties and high-performance material design.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021024] Published Fri May 01, 2026.

motivation: Understanding ion diffusion in superionic conductors is important for designing high-performance materials.
method: The authors use direct spatial and temporal characterization methods to track ion motion.
result: They provide detailed dynamics of ion diffusion in AgCrSe2.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of ion transport in superionic conductors.

title: Cell Bulging And Extrusion In A Three-Dimensional Bubbly Vertex Model For Curved Epithelial Sheets
authors: Oliver M. Drozdowski, Büşra Kocameşe-Tamgac𝚤, Kim E. Boonekamp, Michael Boutros, And Ulrich S. Schwarz

Author(s): Oliver M. Drozdowski, Büşra Kocameşe-Tamgac𝚤, Kim E. Boonekamp, Michael Boutros, and Ulrich S. Schwarz

Cells at topological defects in curved epithelial sheets experience mechanical forces that facilitate extrusion.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021023] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cell bulging and extrusion in curved epithelial sheets using a three-dimensional bubbly vertex model.
motivation: Understanding how mechanical forces at topological defects drive cell extrusion in curved tissues is important for developmental biology and disease.
method: The authors develop a 3D bubbly vertex model to simulate epithelial sheets on curved surfaces and analyze cell shape changes and extrusion events.
result: They find that cells at topological defects experience enhanced mechanical forces that facilitate bulging and extrusion, with curvature playing a key role.
conclusion: The model provides insights into the mechanobiology of epithelial tissues and the role of geometry in cell extrusion.

title: Boosting The Thermoelectric Performance Of $α$-MgAgSb Through Phase-Transition-Induced Self-Doping
authors: Kaiwei Guo, Tianyu Wang, Zhen Fan, Lunhua He, Fuhong Chen, Yi Wang, Qi Zhao, Jiawei Yang, Hangtian Zhu, Jun Li, Te-Huan Liu, And Huaizhou Zhao

A doping-free approach is able to boost thermoelectric performance, providing an attractive route for developing waste heat recovery technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021011] Published Fri Apr 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a doping-free method to enhance thermoelectric performance of α-MgAgSb via phase-transition-induced self-doping.
motivation: To develop an alternative route for waste heat recovery without traditional doping, which often introduces complications.
method: The authors induce a phase transition in α-MgAgSb to create self-doping, and characterize the resulting thermoelectric properties.
result: The self-doping approach significantly boosts the thermoelectric figure of merit (ZT) compared to conventionally doped samples.
conclusion: Phase-transition-induced self-doping is an effective strategy for improving thermoelectric materials without external dopants.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews experimental progress in hadron production from open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and QCD.
motivation: Understanding charmonium decays and searching for new hadrons tests QCD and strong interaction mechanisms.
method: Review of experimental results from BABAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII on e+e- collisions producing open-charm meson pairs.
result: Summarizes current knowledge and highlights recent advances from BESIII in measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems.
conclusion: BESIII has become the leading facility for such measurements, providing high-precision data for hadron spectroscopy.

title: Editorial: A Tribute To The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Véronique van Elewyck And Dietrich Belitz
abstract:
Author(s): Véronique Van Elewyck and Dietrich Belitz

Three Colloquia honor the Arecibo Observatory’s legacy, exploring its revolutionary impact on planetary radar studies, radio astronomy, and geospace science.

[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 010001] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: An editorial tribute to the Arecibo Observatory, summarizing its contributions to planetary radar, radio astronomy, and geospace science.
motivation: To honor the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its impact on multiple scientific fields.
method: The paper is an editorial compilation of colloquia, not a research article with a specific methodology.
result: Highlights the observatory's revolutionary contributions to planetary radar studies, radio astronomy, and geospace science.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory had a profound and lasting impact on science, and its legacy continues to inspire.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the scientific legacy of the planetary radar system at the Arecibo Observatory, focusing on observations of solar system bodies.
motivation: To provide an overview of the unique contributions of Arecibo's planetary radar to planetary science, especially after its upgrade.
method: The paper is a colloquium-style review, summarizing radar techniques and key observational results from Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids.
result: Arecibo's radar provided high-resolution surface and subsurface data, aiding in situ exploration and characterization of asteroids and comets.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system was a uniquely powerful tool for planetary radar astronomy, and its loss leaves a significant gap in capabilities.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A historical review of the Arecibo radio telescope's contributions to radio astronomy and atmospheric science.
motivation: To document the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its scientific impact over five decades.
method: Historical narrative and summary of key scientific results from Arecibo's upgrades and observations.
result: Highlights Arecibo's major contributions to pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
conclusion: Arecibo was a transformative instrument in radio astronomy, and its loss is significant for the field.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews advances in geospace science using the Arecibo Observatory's radar and lidar instruments, focusing on ionospheric physics and space weather.
motivation: To summarize key scientific contributions from the Arecibo Observatory in upper atmospheric and ionospheric research.
method: Review of incoherent scatter radar technique and results from Arecibo's radar, lidar, and optical instruments.
result: Highlights advances in plasma physics, space weather, metal layers, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory enabled unique studies of geospace, but the paper is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: The rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm clouds is poorly understood; controlled experiments are needed.
method: The authors review experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of convection-cloud chambers that reproduce key cloud processes.
result: Convection-cloud chambers can generate turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation, bridging laboratory and atmospheric scales.
conclusion: These chambers offer a promising approach to resolving the precipitation bottleneck in cloud physics.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae and their detection in ground-based interferometers.
motivation: Core collapse supernovae are rare multimessenger events; detecting gravitational waves would provide unique insights into the supernova engine and neutron star formation.
method: The paper summarizes latest progress in supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discusses detection methods and parameter estimation for ground-based laser interferometers.
result: It presents an overview of predicted gravitational wave signatures and the status of detection strategies.
conclusion: Gravitational wave observations from a Galactic supernova would be a landmark event for multimessenger astronomy, but the paper does not advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a cosmological observation that challenges the standard ΛCDM model.
motivation: To test the cosmological principle by comparing the dipole in the large-scale matter distribution with the CMB dipole.
method: Analysis of radio galaxy and quasar catalogs to measure the matter dipole and compare it to the CMB dipole.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the two dipoles, suggesting a possible violation of the cosmological principle.
conclusion: The anomaly may indicate new physics beyond ΛCDM or unknown systematic biases.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala
abstract:
Author(s): Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, and Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: A review of astrophysical tests of dark matter self-interactions, focusing on dark sector models and their observational signatures.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter by testing self-interaction models using astrophysical observations.
method: Review of theoretical predictions and observational constraints from galaxy to large-scale structure scales.
result: Summarizes current constraints on dark matter self-interaction cross sections from various astrophysical probes.
conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable candidate, with ongoing and future observations expected to tighten constraints.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for beyond-Standard Model physics, but recent LHC results have constrained its parameter space, motivating a review of viable models and future discovery potential.
method: The paper surveys current experimental constraints and theoretical developments, and projects discovery potential across multiple search channels at the HL-LHC.
result: Stringent bounds on supersymmetric parameter space are summarized, and projections for HL-LHC sensitivity are provided for various well-motivated scenarios.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains viable but increasingly constrained; the HL-LHC offers significant discovery potential for certain models.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion reactions, plasma physics, and helioseismology.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting solar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models and experimental data from the last decade on nuclear reaction rates, plasma effects, and atomic physics in the solar interior.
result: It summarizes advances in nuclear reaction cross sections, plasma screening, and the impact on solar models.
conclusion: Improved understanding of hydrogen burning enhances predictions of solar properties and neutrino fluxes.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: A review of gas bubble dynamics in liquids, covering turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and surfactants.
motivation: Gas bubbles are ubiquitous in natural and industrial processes, and understanding their dynamics is crucial for modeling two-phase flows.
method: The paper reviews recent advances in experimental and theoretical studies of bubble motion, including effects of deformability, turbulence, and rheology.
result: Key advances over the past 20 years are summarized, highlighting the influence of liquid properties and flow conditions on bubble behavior.
conclusion: The review provides insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.

abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

tldr: This paper reviews the nonlinear elasticity theory of buckling, creases, and cusps in growing soft matter, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding the formation of wrinkles, creases, and cusps in soft materials under compression or growth is important for materials science and biology.

title: Using Gravitational Waves To See The First Second Of The Universe
authors: Rishav Roshan And Graham White
abstract:
Author(s): Rishav Roshan and Graham White

Gravitational waves open a unique window on the earliest times in cosmology because the dense primordial plasma, impenetrable to light or neutrinos, is transparent to gravitational waves up to the instant of the birth of the Universe. This review discusses the possible signals from the phase transitions, topological defects, and other cosmological sources, as well as a range of strategies for detection of the stochastic gravitational waves produced by the earliest events in the history of the Universe.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015001] Published Wed Jan 08, 2025.
tldr: A review of using gravitational waves to probe the early universe, focusing on phase transitions and topological defects.
motivation: Gravitational waves can penetrate the early universe's opaque plasma, offering a unique window into the first second after the Big Bang.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models of gravitational wave sources (phase transitions, topological defects) and detection strategies.
result: It summarizes possible signals and detection methods for stochastic gravitational waves from early universe events.
conclusion: Gravitational wave astronomy can reveal physics of the early universe inaccessible to electromagnetic observations.
